items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,550-1,650 crores and EBITDA of INR240-250 crores excluding inventory and forex gains
items.value: INR1,550-1,650 crores revenue; INR240-250 crores EBITDA
items.quote: For '27, we expect to deliver a revenue of INR1,550 crores to INR1,650 crores with an EBITDA of INR240 crores to INR250 crores, excluding price fluctuation due to geopolitical-led supply chain issues and forex gain/losses, if any.

items.statement: 5-year aspiration to scale revenue to INR2,800-3,000 crores supported by capacity expansions and higher value-added products
items.quote: Further, we aspire to scale the business to INR2,800 crores to INR3,000 crores in the next 5 years, supported by capacity expansions, higher value-added offerings, so we'll go into the higher EBITDA products because, as I said, the groundwork in this last 30 years has been done, and deeper engagement with global customers as we grow from here.

items.statement: Phase 1 capex of INR250-300 crores over next two years for existing products, funded by internal accruals and potential debt
items.quote: We have charted about the capex of about INR250 to INR300 crores as a Phase 1 of our expansion plan towards existing products.

items.statement: Phase 2 capex of INR250-300 crores for new R&D products with better margins, product identification and approvals in progress
items.quote: Phase 2 expansion of nearly INR250 to INR300 crores would be targeting new R&D products with better margins. Product identification, site preparation, and the regulatory approvals are still in the progress.

items.statement: Combined installed capacity of ~98,000 tons per annum; Khopoli at 78,800 tons running at optimum utilization, Mahad at 19,900 tons improved from 13% to 44% utilization
items.quote: On our manufacturing plant, now we have combined installed capacity of about 98,000 tons per annum across our ISO-certified plants, operating on the zero liquid discharge basis. Khopoli plant has about 78,800 tons of capacity, running at optimum utilization in FY26. Mahad, our newer greenfield site with about 19,900 tons of capacity, went through a difficult phase with COVID-related disruptions, a

items.statement: Mahad utilization reached 60%+ in Q1 FY27, expected to reach 70%+ by year-end; 20 acres additional land purchased for future expansion
items.quote: No, it's working beautifully, as I said earlier, that once we got the things in order, the company, from 12% utilization, has moved towards the 60%-plus utilization. Towards the year-end, it will go towards 70-plus.

items.statement: Expansion to add ~60,000 tons capacity (total ~150-160k tons) across Khopoli and Mahad, with projects rolling out over 12-18 months
items.quote: So, basically, if you see, all these 10, 12 projects will come across in the next 12 to 18 months from today. All this money will be spent and in installed. Yes.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin 37.9% vs 30% YoY, boosted by INR25 crores inventory gain; sustainable normalized gross margin range 30-32%
items.quote: Gross margin for the quarter stood at 37.9% compared to 30% in Q1 FY26. Due to the geopolitical-led supply chain issues, there was a sharp increase in average selling price to the tune of INR25 crores positive impact on our gross profit during Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Sustainable gross margins seen at 30-32% normalized, supported by higher value-added mix and operating efficiency
items.quote: Looking beyond the near-term benefit from our higher realization, we see sustainable gross margins in the range of about 30%, 32% on a normalized basis. This is supported by the structural factors, including our higher value-added product mix and operating efficiency from debottlenecking and higher captive consumptions of the intermediates.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 15-16% at year-end
items.quote: The end of the year EBITDA margin, we are talking of 15% to 16% in that range.

items.statement: Volume grew mid-single digits in Q1; demand strong across all sectors; healthy order book from domestic and global customers diversifying supply chains
items.quote: Volume grew in the mid-single digit range, while demand across all the sectors remained strong.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Acetone specialties ~40%, Phosphorus specialties ~40%, Other specialties ~20%; aim to reduce other specialties from 18% to ~10% in 5 years
items.quote: In terms of revenue mix, it continues to remain stable. Acetone-based specialty chemicals contributed nearly 40% of revenue, phosphorus-based specialty chemicals nearly 40%, and the other specialty chemicals the balance 20%.

items.statement: 13 new products commercialized in last 3 years across mining, agro intermediates, lubricant additives, construction emulsifiers; 40 products in R&D pipeline with 15-20% conversion rate
items.quote: On product development front, we have commercialized 13 new products over the last 3 years across the mining chemicals, agro intermediates, lubricant additives, and construction emulsifiers, while we continue to invest in our R&D and developing several products across these segments.

items.statement: INR25 crores allocated for floating roof storage tanks at Khopoli to secure acetone supply; diversifying sourcing with new east coast sources and barge transport
items.quote: If you look at my expansion plan, we have set aside INR25 crores towards the storage tank with floating roof. Floating roof so that the acetone doesn't vaporize. You don't lose the acetone to the vapors. And the company is going to invest in the next one year more than INR25 crores in the adjoining land that we have purchased at Khopoli to store the additional material.

items.statement: Net working capital cycle 50 days at end FY26; average 60-70 days; slightly elevated at year-end due to sales push; comfortable credit terms from suppliers
items.quote: Our net working capital cycle was 50 days at the end of FY26. Working capital discipline remains a key focus area for us, particularly in a very volatile price environment.

items.statement: IPO proceeds INR60 crores used to repay borrowings; net debt-to-equity 0.19x as of March 2026; Phase 1 capex to be funded by internal accruals and potentially additional debt
items.quote: On the IPO, the fresh issue raised gross proceeds of INR80 crores. Of the net proceeds of INR76.4 crores, INR60 crores have already been allocated and utilized to repay borrowings, and INR16.4 crores to general corporate purposes.

items.statement: Geopolitical environment fluid; monitoring crude, marine freight, currency; West Asia conflict reduced some exports but diversification offset impact
items.quote: While geopolitical environment remains fluid, we continue to closely monitor developments across crude, marine freight, currency, and will remain focused on the maintaining the supply chain resilience and serving our customers effectively.

items.statement: Environmental clearance for new products takes 9-12 months; advanced stage for 1-2 products; REACH registration for 6-7 products already obtained
items.quote: Normally, the clearance takes that nine months to a year period. The R&D is done, detailed engineering done, the costing has been done and we are truly at an advanced stage and the land is also marked in terms of utilization of our land, adjoining land, using some of the facilities that we have in the old plant because it is interconnected.

items.statement: All directors long-tenured (25, 19, 15+ years); double graduates with multinational experience; R&D team strengthened with multi-purpose plant and application lab investment
items.quote: You'll be happy to know that all the Directors have been with the company -- like Gaurang has been for 25 years. He started as a summer intern and then went to US, came back to India, and has joined the company ever since and then went up the ladder based on his input to the organization.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 GMV increased to INR193 crores from INR133 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Q1 F Y '27, the GMV increased to INR193 crores from INR133 crores in Q1 of FY '26, while AOV increased from INR66,000 to INR86,000.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin retained at 36% versus Q1 FY26
items.quote: Gross profit also increased to INR43 crores while retaining the gross margin at 36% as compared to Q1 last year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA was negative INR11 crores versus negative INR4 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA stood at negative INR11 crores compared to negative INR4 crores in Q1 of FY '26.

items.statement: Inventory reduced from INR174 crores in Q1 FY26 to INR159 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: At the same time, inventory reduced from INR174 crores in Q1 of FY '26 to INR159 crores, as well as the net working capital reduced from INR105 crores in Q1 of FY '26 to INR66 crores in Q1 of F Y '2 7.

items.statement: Customer advances increased from INR37 crores in Q1 FY26 to INR49 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: But while assessing the performance, the revenue should be adjusted for increase in the advance received from customer, which has gone up from INR37 crores in quarter one of FY '26 to INR49 crores in Q1 of FY '27.

items.statement: No significant expansion planned immediately after four large stores opened in FY26
items.quote: Immediately, there is no significant expansion in sight because we have already done four large stores in las t financial year, so we want that scenario run to happen.

items.statement: Four large-format experience centers opened in FY26: Fort Mumbai, South Ex Delhi, Linking Road Bandra, Madison Avenue New York
items.quote: We opened four large-format experience centers during F Y '26 in Fort and Linking Road and South Ex Delhi and Madison Avenue in New York.

items.statement: Borrowings increased from INR371 crores at FY26 end to INR436 crores at June 2026
items.quote: borrowings increased from INR371 crores at FY '26 end to INR436 crores at June 2026

items.statement: Interest on lease liability and depreciation on right-of-use assets fixed unless store changes made
items.quote: So the interest on lease liability and combined with the depreciation on right of use of assets, that's typically a function of if you do any expansion or make any changes.

items.statement: Other finance costs linked to borrowings; expected to reduce as operational profit accrues
items.quote: Now as far as the other finance costs are concerned, as you said it's linked to the borrowing on the books. The idea is that as we accrue more and more operational profit from the business, that debt can keep on reducing, which would directly affect the other finance costs.

items.statement: Net cash used in operating activities improved from INR55 crores in Q1 FY26 to INR19 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: you can see that the net cash used in operating activities improved from INR55 crores in Q1 of FY '26 to INR19 crores in Q1 of F Y '27, while free cash flow improved from negative INR71 crores last year to negative INR24 crores in Q1 of FY '27.

items.statement: Women's wear above INR1 lakh grew from INR187 crores in FY24 to INR312 crores in FY26; men's wear grew from INR96 crores to INR132 crores; below INR35k women's wear declined from INR162 crores to INR86 crores
items.quote: Now, in the third generation, we are sharpening the focus towards higher-value categories, which has led the 1 lakh plus women's wear generating INR312 crores GMV in FY '26 compared to INR187 crores in FY '24. Men's wear has also grown meaningfully to INR132 crores in FY '26. At the same time, the lower value below 35,000 women's wear has declined from INR162 crores to INR86 crores in F Y '26, ref

items.statement: Top 50,000 customers contributed INR702 crores of INR722 crores GMV in FY26; average GMV per customer rose to INR108,000 in FY26 from INR67,000 in FY24
items.quote: In FY '22, our Top 50,000 customers contributed INR234 crores, which increased to INR702 crores in FY '26. This trajectory is an important part of our third-generation strategy where the focus is increasingly on deepening the wallet share of our customers.

items.statement: Active designer base reduced from 1,910 brands in FY24 to 1,109 brands in FY26 while AOV increased from INR46,000 to INR76,000
items.quote: As a result, we have reduced our active designer base from 1,910 brands in F Y '24 to 1,109 brands in FY '26, while the AOV increased from INR46,000 to INR76,000 in the same period.

items.statement: Gross margin percentage flat across price points; absolute margin higher on high-value items due to same percentage on larger ticket size
items.quote: So hence my point, from an absolute perspective, if I'm operating let's say at an average 40% margin, I'm just giving a number, so selling a INR2 lakh piece gives me INR80,000 margin. Selling a INR20,000 piece gives me only INR8,000 margin. So from an absolute perspective, it's higher margin. But percentage perspective, it completely depends on what markdown I'm working with that brand

items.statement: EBITDA breakeven requires gross profit of INR55 crores per quarter on P&L basis; cash breakeven requires additional INR29 crores GP for lease payments
items.quote: So the calculation, back calculation up to the GP will give you an EBITDA positive straight away there, which basically means if I'm able to grow the GP to INR55 crores, it would convert to a zero EBITDA.

items.statement: Q1 cost structure representative for FY27 unless further expansion; operating leverage expected in subsequent quarters
items.quote: So the Q1 that you see right now is pretty much what we are operating as cost structure today. So I don't see any significant change in that unless we make any change to any of our stores in future, which at the right time we will be notifying.

items.statement: Backorder model contributes ~40-50% of sales; customer advances approx one month of revenue with 45-60 day average delivery
items.quote: So even if you average the products to be in 45 to 60, and currently you can see that usually the advance from customer is approximately one month of revenue, which basically means if at any point of time if we have 45 days average delivery, so that backorder is going to contribute almost close to 40% to 50% of the sales at any point of time.

items.statement: New York store on shorter tenure lease; performance to be observed for 12-18 months before rent decisions
items.quote: It's a June end lease for us. We did a shorter tenure lease to understand how the dynamics would pan out. Depending on how we perform over the first 12, 18 months of business, it's always easy basically to tune your rent up and down.

items.statement: Mumbai GMV grew from INR28 crores to INR50 crores, Delhi from INR29 crores to INR39 crores, Hyderabad from INR10 crores to INR16 crores, USA from INR20 crores to INR29 crores in 3M FY27 vs 3M FY26
items.quote: So , the growth momentum has continued in 3M of F Y '27 versus 3M of F Y '26, with Mumbai's contribution increasing from INR28 crores to INR50 crores, Delhi from INR29 crores to INR39 crores, Hyderabad from INR10 crores to INR16 crores, and USA from INR20 crores to INR29 crores.

items.statement: Revenue from operations increased from INR106 crores in Q1 FY26 to INR119 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: On Slide 19, from financials perspective, revenue from operations increased from INR106 crores in Q1 of F Y '26 to INR119 crores in Q1 of F Y '27.

items.statement: Quarterly numbers can be erratic; advise observing cumulative performance over next few quarters for clarity
items.quote: Now, in our business, the quarterly numbers can sometimes be erratic, so it's important to see them in a cumulative sense. Hence, I would advise as you see more quarterly numbers over the next few quarters, you will get a much better clarity in terms of ho w the inventory will be managed going forward.

items.quote: Apart from this, the company will do a share buyback and a special dividend, the combined allocation towards which, as of now planned, is approximately INR200 crores. So, out of the INR500 crores, almost 80% will be utilized in this manner.

items.quote: And one important thing of about the buyback that you should know is that the promoters will not be participating in it. So the entire buyback will be open only to the public shareholders, which is also adding a lot of value to it.

items.quote: as of now, we are looking for both the chemical and EPC, not more than about INR150 crores in Stage 1. Prateek Kothari: Right. items.quote: And this is demonstrated by the fact that we are already received orders of over 600 tons for export to these regions, and this is expected to grow to almost 2,000 tons per year.

items.statement: EPC order book currently ~INR500 crores with KKR order; next year expected INR500-600 crores; 4-5 year target INR2,500-3,000 crores
items.quote: So Romil, like I already explained, I don't want to speculate on future numbers, but what I can tell you is that next year our order book is expected to be close to about INR500 crores to INR600 crores on EPC. And we expect that in the next 4 to 5 years, we should take that number up to at least INR2,500 crores to INR3,000 crores.

items.quote: This year financially, it's around INR50 crores, INR60 crores because it's a seasonal thing. But from next year onwards, obviously, with this KKR thing, our yearly EPC revenue will be around, along with the other EPC contracts, it will be crossed around INR250 crores per annum.

items.statement: Sufficient funds from deal tranches and business growth to service EPC working capital; banking lines for guarantees to be reinstated
items.quote: But as regards as working capital for the EPC, I believe that the company has sufficient money after the as the tranches come in and as we grow the business to service the working capital requirements. items.quote: We are already in advanced discussion with various technology and license providers to develop certain niche agro and other product derivatives for which we will be setting up our manufacturing capabilities, where th e potential is to go from current -- to double the current turnover of the chemical plants and also double the current profitability of the plant

items.statement: Crude price fluctuations affect petroleum-based raw materials; attempt to pass on to customers; systems in place to sustain reasonable fluctuations
items.quote: So, Saurabh, while you're absolutely right that we are petroleum -based raw materials, so crude fluctuations do affect us, but we try to pass on our fluctuations to our customers as much as possible.

items.quote: In this quarter , in June quarter, chemical has done a turnover of almost 60 crores, and against that, there was a profit of INR6 crores. So at that rate, you can assume that it will continue. So with the existing capacity, we are going to cross 20 crore s this year for chemical

items.quote: EBIT margins in the Wires and Cables segment stood at 14.2%. Margins improved sequentially, supported by a favourable product mix and continued operational excellence initiatives.

items.statement: FMEG EBIT margin crossed double-digit for first time at 10.1% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The segment also achieved a major profitability milestone, with EBIT margins crossing the double-digit mark for the first time and recording a 10.1% margin during the quarter.

items.statement: EPC EBIT margin 7.2% in Q2 FY27 on revenue of INR 6,171 million
items.quote: The EPC segment reported revenues of INR 6,171 million in Q2 FY27, representing a healthy year-on-year growth of 53%. Segment profitability remained strong at INR444 million, translating into an EBIT margin of 7.2%.

items.statement: EPC order book roughly INR 9,000 to 10,000 crores
items.quote: Roughly the order book, I would say it is close to around INR9,000 crores, INR10,000 crores.

items.statement: Strong export order pipeline across US, Europe, LATAM, Asia
items.quote: We are pretty much confident that we have a very strong order book in place in big markets for us, U.S., Europe, LATAM, Asia, all are contributing significantly to us.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capital expenditure INR 6.1 billion for capacity expansion, supply chain capabilities and future growth platforms
items.quote: During the first half of the year, we incurred capital expenditures of INR 6.1 billion, reflecting our ongoing investments in capacity expansion, supply chain capabilities and future growth platforms.

items.statement: EHV plant commissioning expected in FY28
items.quote: We are expecting the EHV plant to now commission somewhere in FY 2028, the next year, though, so FY28.

items.statement: Copper prices up 40-45% on average in H1 FY27; cost-plus model passes through price changes monthly for cables, fortnightly for wires
items.quote: If you see, the copper prices started to tend towards 10,000-12,000 from November or December last year. So there will be some point where the base will also get affected in that.

items.statement: Wires outpaced cables in growth; channel sales grew faster than institutional; premium mix in fans 33%, lights 38%
items.quote: Within the portfolio, wires continued to outpace cables in terms of growth. Channel sales also grew faster than institutional sales, underscoring the resilience and effectiveness of our distribution-led model.

items.statement: FMEG premium mix: fans 33% premium, lights 38% premium driving margin expansion
items.quote: Today, if you see, the fans mix is around 33% in the premium category and the lights also now reaching at 38%. So all of this is actually contributing to the margin growth.

items.statement: Export footprint expanded to 94 countries; added ~10 countries last year; Chile contributed in Q2
items.quote: If you see last year, I think today we are at 94 countries. Last year we added around 10 countries in our portfolio. So we have a very diversified base in terms of exports.

items.statement: UltraTech entry in wires is small portion of INR 1.1 lakh crore market; wires ~30% of market, 30-35% unorganized; no pricing action taken
items.quote: UltraTech's entry, I believe that's the peer that you have been referring to. The entry into a particular category of wires market today is a very small portion of our overall business.

items.statement: No pricing correction seen despite competitor channel checks suggesting 10-15% lower pricing
items.quote: We have a larger set of channel checks and distribution network. We are not seeing any sort of pricing correction right now.

items.statement: Average working capital cycle reduced to ~11 days in Q2 FY27 aided by higher payable days from LC usage; expected to normalize to 45-50 days
items.quote: We also witnessed further improvement in our working capital efficiency, with the average working capital cycle reducing to approximately 11 days in second quarter fiscal '27. This was aided by higher payable days arising from the increased use of letters of credit for our raw material procurement.

items.statement: Net cash INR 45.2 billion as of September 30, 2026 vs INR 29.4 billion a year ago
items.quote: Net cash stood at INR 45.2 billion as of September 30th, 2026, compared to INR 29.4 billion a year ago.

items.statement: Filed appeal before NCLAT against Asier Metals admission order; NCLAT stayed admission order including CIRP initiation; hearing completed October 15, order reserved
items.quote: We have filed an appeal before the Honorable National Company Law Appellate Tribunal, Principal Bench, New Delhi, and the Honorable NCLAT has staye d and kept in abeyance the order of admission in its entirety, including that of it being a commercial dispute of INR 2.79 crores to set aside the order of admission passed by NCLT and initiation of the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process, CIRP, ag

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions, commodity volatility, logistics disruptions may influence individual quarters; Trump trade policy risk noted for exports
items.quote: While commodity volatility, geopolitical developments, and logistics -related disruptions may continue to influence individual quarters, the structural drivers of the demand remain firmly intact and in place.

items.statement: Wires and Cables volume growth mid-to-high single digit; wires early double-digit, cables mid-single digit volume growth
items.quote: We delivered a volume growth of mid -to high single -digit range on top of a strong base from the corresponding quarter last year, demonstrating the underlying strength of demand. Within the portfolio, wires continued to outpace cables in terms of growth.

items.statement: 100% copper imported; no current plans for domestic sourcing; happy with existing arrangements
items.quote: Today, we are doing 100% of imported copper, and market dynamics suggest today that it's beneficial for us doing this. We never know how the mix is going to go in future. Nobody knows the sourcing part of it.

items.statement: Reiterated confidence in strong double-digit consolidated revenue growth for FY27
items.quote: Based on our first-half performance, continued program ramp-ups, and healthy pipeline conversion, we remain confident in maintaining strong double-digit growth for FY27.

items.statement: Reiterated expectation of delivering double-digit consolidated growth for full year
items.quote: Accordingly, we reiterate our expectation of delivering double-digit consolidated growth for the full year while continue to drive sustainable margin improvements and long-term value creation for our stakeholders.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin remained resilient at 16.1% despite 100+ bps headwind from salary increments
items.quote: Despite absorbing annual salary increments, representing more than a 100-basis-point headwind, operating EBITDA margins remained resilient at 16.1%, reflecting continued execution discipline and the strength of our operating model.

items.statement: Expect sequential margin improvement in second half through disciplined execution and productivity initiatives
items.quote: Against this backdrop, we expect to deliver sequential margin improvement through disci plined execution and productivity initiatives

items.statement: Committed to 18% and 20% as North Star margin targets
items.quote: You know, we have positioned 18% and 20% as the North Star for our company. We'll continue to keep you informed of progress as we work through the year.

items.statement: Secured five large deals in Q2 including landmark US$138 million full vehicle engineering program with European luxury OEM
items.quote: Pipeline conversion remains strong, with five large deals secured during Q2. These included a landmark US$138 million full vehicle engineering program with a leading European luxury automotive OEM, spanning two vehicle programs.

items.statement: Secured engagement with North American commercial vehicle manufacturer for end-to-end new vehicle platform development and digital SDV infrastructure
items.quote: We also secured an engagement with a leading North American commercial vehicle manufacturer to lead the end-to-end development of a new vehicle platform and support the associated digital SDV infrastructure.

items.statement: BMW JV share of profit increased 20% sequentially and 115% year-on-year to INR 11.4 crores
items.quote: In Quarter two, our share of profit from BMW TechWorks India increased 20% sequentially and 115% year-on-year to INR 11.4 crores.

items.statement: Automotive growing 7.6% QoQ excluding ES-Tec, non-automotive grew 7.5% sequentially in USD terms
items.quote: Growth was broad-based, with automotive growing 7.6% QoQ, excluding ES-Tec, while non-automotive grew 7.5% sequentially in US dollar terms.

items.statement: ES-Tec demand remains subdued from largest customer in Germany, anticipate additional softness in Q3, expect stabilization in 2027
items.quote: Demand at ES-Tec remains subdued, particularly from its largest customer in Germany. While we anticipate some additional softness in Q3, we expect conditions to stabilize in 2027 and remain confident in the underlying strength of the business and its medium- to long-term growth prospects.

items.statement: Aerospace demand remains strong with structural tailwinds from commercial aircraft backlog and new programs
items.quote: Demand across the aerospace sector remains strong while the industry continues to face challenges in engineering capacity, production throughput, and manufacturing efficiency.

items.statement: Invested in new office facility in Pune to consolidate operations and create capacity for future growth
items.quote: During the quarter, we invested in a new office facility in Pune to consolidate our operations and create capacity for future growth.

items.statement: Added approximately 300 associates to support strategic program ramp-ups and strengthen key capabilities
items.quote: During this quarter, we added approximately 300 associates to support strategic program ramp-ups and strengthen key capabilities across the business.

items.statement: Total headcount stood at 12,895 associates, net increase of 316 employees or 2.5% sequentially
items.quote: Our total headcount stood at 12,895 associates at the end of the quarter, representing a net increase of 316 employees or 2.5% sequentially.

items.statement: Trailing 12 months voluntary attrition improved to 15.6%, down 70 bps sequentially
items.quote: At the same time, attrition reduced by 70 basis points sequentially to 15.6%, reflecting the progress we are making in employee experience, career development, and engagement.

items.statement: Delivered over 27,000 learning hours and trained more than 5,000 associates across technical and professional skill areas
items.quote: During the quarter, we delivered over 27,000 learning hours and trained more than 5,000 associates across technical and professional skill areas.

items.statement: Services revenue grew 4.3% QoQ and 26.2% YoY to US$142 million, contributing ~80% of total revenue
items.quote: Services revenue grew 4.3% sequentially and 26.2% year-on-year to US$142 million, contributing approximately 80% of our total revenue.

items.statement: Technology Solutions grew 9.2% YoY but declined 6.6% sequentially due to education timing and SaaS revenue recognition change
items.quote: Technology Solutions grew 9.2% year-over-year in constant currency while declining 6.6% sequentially to INR 343 crores. The sequential decline was primarily driven by the timing of revenue recognition in education business and a change in accounting treatment for certain OEM-hosted SaaS license within the product business.

items.statement: DSO at 102 days vs 97 days previous quarter; billed DSO improved to 63 from 65 days, unbilled DSO increased to 39 from 32 days
items.quote: Our DSO stood at 102 days at the end of Q2 compared with 97 days in the previous quarter. Our billed DSO came in at 63 days compared with 65 days in Q1, an improvement, while the unbilled DSO were at 39 days compared to 32 days.

items.statement: Net cash position at INR 330 crores vs INR 880 crores end of Q1, reduction driven by INR 475 crores dividend payout
items.quote: At the end of Q2, our net cash position stood at approximately INR 330 crores compared to INR 880 crores at the end of Q1. The sequential reduction was primarily driven by the dividend payout of nearly INR 475 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: Paid dividend of nearly INR 475 crores during Q2
items.quote: The sequential reduction was primarily driven by the dividend payout of nearly INR 475 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: Competing primarily with European ESPs for global full vehicle programs, seldom see Indian ESP competition outside India
items.quote: But when we are competing in China, when we're competing in Europe, and when we're competing in North America, it's typically th e European ESPs that we compete with. Seldom do we see any competition from the Indian ESPs, at least at this point in time

items.statement: Automotive revenue excluding ES-Tec grew ~16% YoY in Q2
items.quote: And, Mayank, maybe the question that you asked, auto excluding ES-Tec Y-o-Y is about 16%.

items.statement: Germany market weakness from OEM restructuring (VW 100k headcount reduction, BMW VRS) but BMW continues investing in India JV
items.quote: I think VW have announced that they are looking to reduce headcount by 100,000 people between now and 2030, and more recently, BMW have announced a VRS scheme in Germany. I think what's significant is that, despite the fact that BMW are reducing headcount in Germany, they continue to invest in their global R&D footprint that includes the joint venture that we have with them in India.

items.statement: Humanoid/physical AI area of interest with POCs underway but not expected to be material in next 12-18 months
items.quote: As far as humanoids are concerned and physical AI, it's an area of great interest. We are studying the implications that will represent in terms of future opportunity. There are POCs and capabilities that we are investing in inside of our organization, but it's not an area that we expect to represent material opportunity in the short term.

name: Sri Lotus Developers and Realty Ltd

items.statement: FY27 pre-sales guidance of INR1,800-2,000 crores with revenue and PAT growth of 55-60% over FY26
items.quote: Together with the momentum from our recent launches and a growing pipeline, we remain confident of delivering our FY27 guideline of pre -sales in the range of INR1,800 crores to INR2,000 crores, along with revenue and PAT growth of 55% to 60% over FY26 levels.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 35-40% and PAT margin guidance 25-30%
items.quote: We also remain confident of sustaining strong profitability, with EBITDA and PAT margin expected at 35% to 40% and 25% to 30%, respectively.

items.statement: Three new projects added with GDV of INR2,700-2,800 crores, total pipeline now 24 projects with ~INR20,000 crores GDV
items.quote: We also made significant progress on business development during the quarter. Three new projects added, Lotus Impressa at Shivaji Park in Dadar West, Lotus Stellar in Versova, and Lotus Supremus in Juhu, which adds INR2,700 to INR2,800 crores of GDV to existing GDV pipeline.

items.statement: Four H2 FY27 launches planned with combined GDV of INR3,500-4,000 crores
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are well-prepared for the second half. We plan to launch four projects, Lotus Aurelia, Lotus Sky Plaza, Lotus Portofino, and Lotus Odyssey, with a combined estimated GDV of INR3,500 to INR4,000 crores.

items.statement: Luxury segment demand driven by end-users upgrading, less sensitive to rate hikes
items.quote: Demand is driven largely by end users upgrading to larger homes in better locations, while scarce land in prime micromarkets makes redevelopment the principal route to new supply, precisely where Lotus has built its capability.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 39.9%, H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 38.8%, PAT margin 33.5%
items.quote: In Q2, total revenue rose 53% year-on-year to INR269 crores. EBITDA more than doubled to INR107 crores, with margins expanding to 39.9%.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 pre-sales INR470 crores up 83% YoY, H1 FY27 pre-sales INR879 crores up 176% YoY
items.quote: Delighted to share that we recorded pre-sales for the quarter at INR470 crores, up 83% year-on-year. For H1 FY27, pre-sales stood at INR879 crores, up 176% year-on-year.

items.statement: Lotus Trident contributed INR178 crores pre-sales in first full quarter
items.quote: Lotus Trident in Andheri West, our luxury commercial offering, has been a standout performer, contributing pre-sales of INR178 crores in its first full quarter since its launch at the end of June.

items.statement: Q2 collections INR60 crores, H1 collections INR209 crores; expect pickup as projects reach billing milestones
items.quote: Collections stood at INR60 crores for the quarter and INR209 crores for the first half. Collections in our business are linked to construction milestones and can vary from quarter -to-quarter.

items.statement: Two projects reaching plinth level in H2, expect better collections; three project completions in FY28 to drive 95-100% collection
items.quote: So, from the next half yearly, we are confident we'll get good collection because out of three projects, two projects will be out of the basement, and the collection will be improved.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR494 crores as of September 30, 2026; net debt-free
items.quote: As of 30th September 2026, we had a net cash position of INR494 crores. This provides us with the financial flexibility to fund our ongoing projects, support upcoming launches, and pursue new development opportunity, while maintaining a disciplined capital structure.

items.statement: IPO proceeds INR732 crores net, INR550 crores earmarked for subsidiary projects, INR305 crores deployed by September 2026
items.quote: We raised approximately INR792 crores through the fresh issue of our IPO, with net proceeds of approximately INR732 crore s after issue expenses, of which INR550 crore s earmarked for our subsidiary for the Amalfi, Arcadian, and Varun. INR305 crore s had been deployed as on 30th September 2026.

items.statement: Project cycle 2.5-3.5 years; 90% approvals in place for four H2 launches
items.quote: More or less 90% approvals are in place right now. So we are very confident that in H2 that four projects will be able to launch.

items.statement: Price appreciation seen across almost all projects; premium pricing strategy for new launches
items.quote: Almost all the projects, I would say. All the projects.

items.statement: Timeline shifts for Lotus Monarch (1 year) and Ghatkopar Salona due to multi-party approvals; conservative timelines given
items.quote: Regarding this the timeline, because this is a continuous process, and some regulatory and approvals are required. So, in the two projects, we have shifted the timeline. One is the Lotus Monarch, we shifted for one year because there are three, four parties are involved.

items.statement: Commercial redevelopment growing; 5 commercial projects in portfolio; Trident margins similar to guided 33-35% EBITDA
items.quote: And I think we are the only one right now in the suburbs who has completed redevelopment in commercial space. And we have delivered that last year. It's called Arc One. And now, we have taken about two to three projects of redevelopment in commercial space also.

items.statement: Project-level surplus estimated at INR9,500 crores over development cycle of INR20,000 crores GDV portfolio
items.quote: In addition, our estimated project-level surplus stands at approximately INR9,500 crores over the development cycle of our portfolio.

items.statement: Operating cash flow may not turn positive soon due to new project launches consuming cash while existing projects generate collections
items.quote: Whilst the same, when launching new projects, there will be more consumption of cash flow. So it will be a net effect. But we have a good balance in books, and we don't see any kind of deficiency or anything in that.

items.statement: Continuous project additions expected every quarter; talks ongoing with several societies
items.quote: So this is going to be, as this is going to be a continuous process. Right now, we are in talks with couple of societies already. Some we are shortlisted also. So every quarter, yes, we will be adding some projects.

items.statement: Amara and Athena projects at RCC stage; expect OC by March 2027 for both
items.quote: So in the Amara, we have completed the RCC, and we hope that this quarter we will get OC, otherwise, this financial year definitely, as predicted, will get the OC. Athena also, we are in the RCC stage, and we are hopeful that before March, we'll get OC in the Athena.

items.statement: GIFT City project: 5.5-acre land parcel, mixed-use development of 1.3-1.5 million sq ft pending town planning scheme approval
items.quote: It's a 5.5-acre land parcel, which is sitting right on the river Sabarmati. It's in GIFT area. Recently GIFT authority has acquired in a way 300 acres, and this plot is part of that. This will be an ownership land only, and GIFT City would be planning authority in this.

items.statement: Prabhadevi project seeing good inquiries but slower conversion due to premium pricing and new micromarket; expect traction post-plinth
items.quote: For us, it's a new micromarket. Second, we are sitting tight on what our expectation is, because this is a very, very unique project, which has got almost 270 degree of direct sea view, and our pricing is little more premium pricing.

items.statement: Only developer in suburbs to complete commercial redevelopment (Arc One); competitive advantage in redevelopment credibility
items.quote: And I think we are the only one right now in the suburbs who has completed redevelopment in commercial space. And we have delivered that last year. It's called Arc One.

items.statement: Credit growth guidance of 18-20% for FY27
items.quote: With the spurt in credit growth scenario in the industry, we would tread cautiously and look for calibrated growth of 18% to 20% for this financial year.

items.statement: NIM guidance revised to 4% plus for FY27
items.quote: So in view of what we have said earlier and some sort of visibility what we had and considering our pricing methodology of the loan book also, so we may end up above 4% or 4% plus NIM for the full year.

items.statement: ROA guidance of more than 2% for FY27
items.quote: We expect ROA for the full year to be more than 2%.

items.statement: GNPA expected less than 1.5% and NNPA less than 1% for FY27
items.quote: Our GNPA expected to be less than 1.5% and NNPA will be less than 1% and slippages will be less than 1% of our outlook coming to our cost-to-income ratio also.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected below 45% in next two quarters
items.quote: So we feel that we will be below 45% in the next 2 quarters to come.

items.statement: Q2 NIM maintained at 4.26%, 4.34% including one-off recovery
items.quote: I am pleased to report that we were able to maintain our net interest margin at 4.26% for this quarter also. If you look at including the one -off recovery, so interest recovery, 8 basis points from the written -off accounts, it comes to 4.34%.

items.statement: Yield on advances increased 8 bps to 10.09% in Q2
items.quote: The yield on advances increased by 8 basis points during this quarter and remained at 10.09%.

items.statement: Cost of deposits increased 4 bps sequentially in Q2
items.quote: The cost of deposits increased marginally by 4 basis points on a sequential basis as rates of deposits were increased during the first quarter.

items.statement: Funding costs likely under upward pressure for next 2-3 months
items.quote: Funding costs are likely to remain under upward pressure due to RBI's policy tightening, liquidity absorption and competition for deposits.

items.statement: NIM may trend down from 4.26% but will stay above 4%
items.quote: So 4.26% retention that I cannot say anything on that. So -- but 4% and above, I can assure.

items.statement: Advances grew 7% QoQ to INR1,11,589 crores in Q2
items.quote: Advances rose to INR1,11,589 crores representing a growth of 7% quarter -on-quarter.

items.statement: Deposits grew 5% QoQ to INR1,28,123 crores in Q2
items.quote: Deposits increased to INR1,28,123 crores, achieving quarter-on-quarter growth rate of 5%.

items.statement: CASA grew INR1,489 crores in Q2, current account up 5%, savings up 4%
items.quote: Consequently, CASA balance increased by INR1,489 crores during Q2, supported by strong traction in operating accounts, transaction banking relationships.

items.statement: Retail term deposits grew 6% QoQ, INR3,902 crores growth
items.quote: Retail term deposits witnessed healthy traction, supported by calibrated pricing actions undertaken to fund advances growth while maintaining a disciplined approach towards wholesale funding.

items.statement: FCNRB deposits of INR680 crores sourced in Q2
items.quote: The RBI's relaxation on FCNRB interest rate ceilings has enabled the bank to source incremental FCNRB deposits of around INR680 crores during this quarter.

items.statement: RAM segment 86% of advances, corporate 14% in Q2
items.quote: The composition of our advances portfolio remained broadly stable during the quarter with RAM segment continuing to account for 86% of the portfolio and the corporate segment contributed to the remaining 14%.

items.statement: Commercial segment grew 8% QoQ, disbursements up ~24% QoQ
items.quote: The Commercial business segment continued to demonstrate an 8% growth over the previous quarter, driven by higher disbursements in both small business group and business banking group. So it comes to around 24% quarter -on-quarter, we can say the disbursement growth.

items.statement: Retail advances up 5% QoQ, mortgage loans up 12%, personal loans up 11%
items.quote: Retail advances increased by 5% quarter -on-quarter, primarily driven by growth in mortgage loans and personal loans, sequentially down by 1% over the previous quarter. Mortgage loans registered a growth of 12% over the previous quarter. Personal loans grew by 11% over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Retail jewel loans declined 1% QoQ due to calibrated pricing
items.quote: Retail jewel loans marginally declined by 1% during the quarter. We did not reduce the pricing in retail jewel loan segment to have a calibrated growth and hence, declined sequentially.

items.statement: Credit substitutes grew INR500 crores in Q2, focus on A-rated ETB customers
items.quote: We continued our focus on credit substitutes and had a growth of around INR500 crores during the quarter. Our focus would be on ETB customers with an external rating of A and above on this segment.

items.statement: Gross slippages INR123 crores (0.44% annualized), down from INR138 crores
items.quote: Gross slippages for the quarter amounted to INR123 crores, representing 0.44% annualized, 0.11% of the loan book sequentially; it is lower from INR138 crores.

items.statement: GNPA 0.69%, NNPA 0.18%, both improved sequentially
items.quote: Owing to reduce slippages, improved recoveries and upgrades as well as write -offs, our gross NPAs declined marginally by 5 basis points to 0.69%. Our net NPA reduced by 1 basis point to 0.18%.

items.statement: Standard restructured loans 0.33% of total loans, 40.1% provision coverage
items.quote: The proportion of our standard restructured loan portfolio has further decreased to 0.33% of our total loans and continues to perform satisfactorily. Notably, a substantial portion is secured by collateral and we also maintained a provision of 40.1% for the standard restructured loan portfolio.

items.statement: Total provisions to advances at 1.65%, adequate for ECL transition
items.quote: The total provisions to advances is at 1.65%, which should take care of the transition.

items.statement: Credit cost 0.43% annualized in Q2
items.quote: During the quarter under review, an allocation of INR94 crores was made towards NPA migrations, standard assets, restructured assets and INR25 crores additionally, we have provided towards the floating provisions, resulting in a credit cost of 0.43% on an annualized basis.

items.statement: Opened 20 branches in H1 FY27, plan 50 for full year, 26 by December
items.quote: We opened 20 branches, including 2 branches in the first quarter during the half year ended September 2026. We have planned for opening 50 branches during the current financial year, and we would be completing 26 branches before the end of next quarter and balance before the year-end.

items.statement: CRAR Basel III at 17.97%, LCR at 129% (target 115-120%)
items.quote: Our CRAR Basel III continues to be healthy and is at 17.97%, providing us comfortable headroom for growth. Our liquidity coverage ratio for the quarter is at 129%, and we would be maintaining this in the range of 115% to 120%.

items.statement: EBLR book increased to 57% of loan book, fixed rate 34%, MCLR 7%
items.quote: EBLR book increased from 55% to 57% compared to the previous quarter. The fixed rate loan book remained at 34% and MCLR-linked book reduced from 9% to 7%.

items.statement: Operating profit INR1,162 crores, up 14% YoY and 6% QoQ
items.quote: The operating profit for the quarter was at INR1,162 crores, reflecting a 14% increase compared to the same quarter in the previous year and 6% growth sequentially.

items.statement: Net profit INR788 crores, up 37% YoY and 4% QoQ
items.quote: Net profit for the quarter was INR788 crores, an increase of 4% quarter -on-quarter and 37% year -on-year.

items.statement: Outlook vulnerable to geopolitical developments, energy volatility, weather uncertainties
items.quote: The outlook remains vulnerable to geopolitical developments, volatility in global energy markets and weather -related uncertainties. Weak monsoons, coupled with strong El Niño, protracted geopolitical tensions, rising international commodity prices, additional frictions in the global trade and tightening of global financial conditions could adversely impact the growth outlook.

items.statement: Textile portfolio working capital utilization at 76-79%, US export segment only 55-56%
items.quote: Our working capital utilization for the last 1, 1.5 years is in the range of 76% to 79%. It is not going up, same level it is there. Now here, when our textile portfolio is 5. 05 percentage is there, where major portion is there. There, we have further analyzed this particular portion. We look at it where U.S.-based exports are there, there the utilization is around 55%, 56% only.

items.statement: Vehicle financing portfolio declining, tactical shift to mortgages and gold loans
items.quote: we Classification | CONFIDENTIAL thought after looking at all these products, it is a tactical call taken by us. This money is better we place in mortgages and jewel loans

items.statement: No plan for second ED, board search committee formed for CEO succession
items.quote: Second ED, another ED, we have not even thought of not required. Board is equally abreast of looking for the successor. So they are working both internal as well as external candidates and all. So, a search committee has already been formed.

items.statement: NIM target 8%+ long term, 8.2%+ near term; aim to hold NIM in narrow range over next couple of quarters
items.quote: the real aim in the long term we obviously want to be at 8% + . We would want to hold on to where we are as at Q2, and really come up to an 8.2 %+ at least in the near term.

items.statement: Credit cost target 2.3% +/- range for full year
items.quote: in the medium term, what we have said is we would want to manage the credit cost in the range of 2.3% +/- and which is why it's 5 bps up this quarter.

items.statement: ROA target 2.5%+ annualized in short to medium term
items.quote: we would focus on making sure we consistently are able to deliver at a 2.5% o n an annual basis in terms of Ro A that we have spoken about in the short to medium term

items.statement: Expect AUM growth to accelerate towards 17-18% by Q4 FY27
items.quote: I am very hopeful that we should be moving pretty much in that direction and hopeful that Q4 starts to show that in terms of direction.

items.statement: Festive season and post-monsoon pickup expected to drive strong H2 disbursements across verticals
items.quote: Conversations with our channel and OEM partners indicate strong confidence on the back of festive demand, and we look forward to a strong H2.

items.statement: Q2 disbursements grew 18.7% YoY to ₹18,522 crores; gross loan book grew 11.7% YoY to ₹1,24,469 crores
items.quote: Disbursements for the quarter ende d September 30, 2026, was ₹18,522 crores, up 18.7% YoY.  Gross loan book, as at September 30, 2026, stood at ₹1,24,469 crores, growing 11.7% year-on-year and 2.2% sequentially

items.statement: NIM at 8.23% in Q2 FY27 vs 7.95% YoY and 8.35% QoQ; cost-to-income improved to 39.3% from 40.7% YoY

items.statement: Q3 and Q4 order book looks robust, on track for 15% volume growth
items.quote: But as far as we are concerned, as I was telling that our quarter 3, quarter 4 order book looks robust, and we are well on track to get that 15% volume growth for the year.
