items.statement: ECL models will take 1.5-2 years to stabilize; regulator may challenge assumptions
items.quote: I will wait and watch for one year, because this is a new concept. It will take 1.5-2 years for the models to stabilize. They will be challenged, there will be a lot of discussion, and the regulator may not accept all our assumptions.

items.statement: MCLR-linked book 43.19%, external benchmark-linked 49.65%; repo rate hike benefit started immediately on external benchmark book
items.quote: The MCLR-linked book constitutes 43.19% of advances, and the external benchmark-linked book constitutes 49.65%. As you all know, the repo rate has been increased by 25 basis points, so we should see NIM expansion of perhaps 5-6 basis points going forward.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book at Rs 7,237 crore as of 30 Sep 2026, up 32% YoY, executable over 18-24 months
items.quote: As of 30th September 2026, our unexecuted order book stood at 7,237 crore, up by 32% year-on-year, providing strong revenue visibility over the medium term. The order book is executable over the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Order inflows of Rs 1,169 crore in Q2 FY27, 97% YoY growth
items.quote: During Q2 FY27, we received order inflows of 1,169 crores, 97% year-on-year growth over low base of last year this time.

items.statement: Rs 21,000 crore of inquiries under negotiation, 80% domestic and 20% export, equal government-private mix
items.quote: We currently have 21,000 crores of inquiries under negotiation, of which bidding for 80% is domestic orders and 20% export orders, with equal mix between the government and private customers, with utilities and industrial customers.

items.statement: Confident of achieving FY27 guidance of 25% revenue growth and 9-10% PAT margin
items.quote: Following our Q2 performance, we remain confident of achieving FY27 guidance and continue to remain on track with our growth plans for the full year.

items.statement: Maintain FY27 guidance of 25% revenue growth and 9-10% PAT margin
items.quote: So, our target is to reach a growth of 25% and beyond. So, we are keeping it the same.

items.statement: Changodar expansion capex around Rs 150 crore, adding 25,000 MVA capacity to reach 35,000 MVA total
items.quote: Capex is around INR150 odd crores.

items.statement: Changodar plant capacity expanding from 12,000 MVA to 35,000 MVA, commercial production expected around Diwali
items.quote: Total manufacturing capacity at Changodar will be 35,000 MVA. Changodar will be producing distribution transformers, transformers IDT transformers, transform ers for renewable energy

items.statement: Total capacity to reach 75,000 MVA after Changodar expansion
items.quote: So, this will take our total capacity to 75,000? Mehul Shah: Yes

items.statement: Target capacity utilization of 90%, currently working towards it
items.quote: So ideally, I would want a capacity utilization of about 90%, and we are constantly working and we are constantly progressing towards that.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 16.1% vs 8.8% YoY and 13.3% QoQ, driven by operating leverage and utilization
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 16.1% compared to 8.8% in Q2FY26 and 13.3% in Q1 FY27. This reflects the benefit of higher operating leverage and improved utilization level during the quarter.

items.statement: Backward integration expected to add 200-300 bps margin expansion, full effect by FY29
items.quote: So, we are looking at around 200 basis point to 300 basis point margin expansion through this backward integration.

items.statement: Raw material prices (transformer oil, CRGO) remain high but majority of orders have price variation clauses limiting margin impact
items.quote: Yes. So sir, the prices, etcetera, are still on the higher side. But what we have, we have a majority of order which is having, say, a price variation clause. So mainly, it does not affect our margin in a big way.

items.statement: Net working capital days at 154 days (inventory 93, receivables 117, payables 56), target to reduce to 110-120 days
items.quote: Net working capital days stood at around 154 days, comprising inventory days of approximately 93 days, receivable days of around 117 days, and payable days of approximately 56 days.

items.statement: Target working capital cycle of 110-120 days by end of FY27 to generate positive free cash flow
items.quote: It should be below 120 days. We are trying to, you know, reach at 120, and once we reach there, we would like to see close to between 110 days and 120 days this year.

items.statement: Standalone debt Rs 575 crore (long-term Rs 125 cr, short-term Rs 449 cr), debt/equity 0.35x, cash Rs 77 cr
items.quote: On a standalone basis, tot al debt stood at approximately INR575 crores, comprising long -term borrowing of around INR125 crores and short-term borrowing for around INR449 crores. The debt to equity ratio stood at approximately 0.35x

items.statement: Exports 8% of Q2 FY27 revenue, 15% of order book
items.quote: So in Q2 FY27, our export is around 8% of the total revenue. And in the order book also, we have around roughly around 15-odd percentage with the export.

items.statement: Order book 55-60% high voltage (400 kV+), Q2 execution 56% power transformers
items.quote: Roughly we have around 55% of order which is having a high voltage class. 55% to 60% is a high voltage class, 400 kV and above.

items.statement: First nuclear order for NPCIL Kaiga Units 5&6 (400 kV+ generator transformers), repetitive in nature
items.quote: First-ever order of nuclear power sector, supplying generator transformers for NPCIL Kaiga Units 5 and 6, marking the strategic entry into high-level infrastructure and high-value infrastructure segment

items.statement: Nuclear transformer content 15-18% of greenfield nuclear project cost
items.quote: So, greenfield nuclear new projects would be close to about 15% to 18%.

items.statement: Major orders: NPCIL (nuclear), Megha Engineering (35-month execution), APTRANSCO (13-month), DVC (15-28 month), GETCO (24-30 month)
items.quote: Major orders we received during this quarter were:  First-ever order of nuclear power sector, supplying generator transformers for NPCIL Kaiga Units 5 and 6, marking the strategic entry into high -level infrastructure and high -value infrastructure segment  Received large transformer order from Megha Engineering and Infrastructures Limited in August 2026 with execution scheduled over the next 35

items.statement: Competes with Kanohar in 132-220 kV segment; no major price war as competitors have full order books
items.quote: As far as Kanohar is concerned, yes, we do compete with them in the segments of 132 kV and 220 kV.

items.statement: NPCIL Kaiga order won against Crompton and other large manufacturers
items.quote: The NPCIL order for Kaiga project, we were c ompeting with Crompton and other large transformer manufacturers

items.statement: Average realization ~Rs 7 lakh per MVA across transformer types
items.quote: On an average, we will be realizing around INR7 lakhs per MVA.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 production ~9,500 MVA
items.quote: It is roughly 9,500 MVA.

items.statement: Backward integration plants (CTC, pressboard, bushings, tanks) progressing; CTC plant commissioning by Diwali, commercial production Q4 FY27, 60% captive consumption
items.quote: In Q3, before Diwali the plant will be commissioned. Currently, the plant and machinery is being installed. By Diwali, the plant will be commissioned. in November and then December, we will do the first trial runs. And by qu arter four this year, we should be commercially manufacturing CTC

items.statement: Moraiya EHV expansion to start after Changodar completion, 30% capacity addition from freed insulation space, target FY28 production
items.quote: And pl us what will happen with our insulation and pressboard plant com ing live, the manufacturing place for insulation, which was at Moraiya, will now be added to transformer manufacturing unit. So, we will be adding about 30% plus manufacturing capacity at Moraiya

items.statement: USD 1 billion revenue target by late FY29 or early 2030, includes transformer + backward integration product sales, no additional capex needed
items.quote: It will be late part of FY29 or early 2030.

items.statement: HVDC converter transformer qualification 1.5 years away (repair 4-5 months, testing 6-7 months, then tender participation)
items.quote: So, we are currently repairing the transformer, so with that will be another four to five months' time, then the successful running of that transformer will take another six to seven months. And then we will qualify for the manufacturing, and then we will start participating into the tender. So at least one and one and half months one and half year is away from when we are speaking.

items.statement: BESS transformer inquiries ongoing, expect orders in current quarter, market assessment underway
items.quote: No. We are not currently executing any BESS pipeline. But yes, there are inquiries that are currently ongoing, and we are sure that in this quarter we should get some orders for BESS transformers.

items.statement: Registered supplier for large data center facilities in India and abroad, 20% of inquiries export-linked
items.quote: We are registered manufacturers for a lot of large data center facilities, so we have a preference there.

items.statement: Retention money ~5-10% of orders, currently ~Rs 200 crore on balance sheet
items.quote: Roughly, it would be around INR200 crores.

items.statement: Management expects festive shift of ~INR40 crore advertising revenue from Q2 to Q3 FY27 and remains optimistic on next two quarters despite geopolitical concerns
items.quote: we believe there is an impact of almost around INR40 crores. Now with that shifting into Q3 and the overall momentum, what we believe is there, though in certain parts of India, the monsoon is not playing well because in Rajasthan, even there's a rains happening even today.

items.statement: Management endeavors to achieve high single-digit to early double-digit full-year advertising revenue growth
items.quote: That's what our endeavor is. Looking at this -- what we've seen in the last 7, 8 days of festival, overall momentum is good. let's hope this continues.

items.statement: Festive season shift (Navratri moved from Q2 to Q3) impacted YoY advertising comparison; underlying advertising revenue grew positive single-digit excluding festive shift
items.quote: As you know, last year, Navaratra festival season was in Q2, and this year, it falls in Q3. So on a like -to-like basis, D. B. Corp advertising revenue and EBITDA registered positive single -digit growth in Q2 excluding the impact of this festive shift.

items.statement: Real estate advertising flat to single-digit; jewelry strong double-digit; banking/financial services and IPO advertising up ~50% (small base); healthcare strong double-digit; auto flat; education single-digit; FMCG down 2% YoY but ~single-
items.quote: Real estate single digit, ideally, this should have been good double digit, but because of the real festival season going this way. So most of them are almost flat or single digit.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA INR124 crore vs INR115 crore YoY; PAT INR69 crore vs INR93 crore YoY; H1 EBITDA INR289 crore vs INR297 crore YoY
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR124 crores compared to INR115 crores in the corresponding quarter last year, while profit after tax stood at INR69 crores against INR93 crores.

items.statement: Newsprint cost per tonne increased ~21% YoY from INR47,000 to ~INR57,000 due to geopolitical situation; domestic prices follow imported; freight also higher; expects 2-3% softening in Q3-Q4
items.period: Q2 FY27, Q3 FY27, Q4 FY27
items.quote: What we were paying INR47,000 per tonne average cost, we are paying right now almost INR57,000. So there are almost 20.8% to be more precise 21% is the impact on the newsprint cost.

items.statement: Inventory: few months for domestic paper (10-15 days transit), around a quarter for imported paper
items.quote: Inventory generally speaking, we keep a few months for the Indian because Indian transportation takes 10 to 15 days maximum and imported around a quarter.

items.statement: No cover price hikes planned; increasing cover price would accelerate circulation decline; average monthly consumer cost INR150-170 (net ~INR100 after waste recovery)
items.quote: We have taken this call, if you remember, a year back or so, that overall, let's face it, the re is a change on the number of copies. And furthermore, if we increase the cover price, that will further accelerate the decline. So we don't want to do that

items.statement: Advertising pricing: upgrading advertisers from inside pages to premium pages (front, back, third page) to increase ticket size; no discount on premium page rates
items.quote: What we are doing on the pric ing side, we are able to increase the ticket size, which means the advertiser who was advertising on inside page, we've been able to upgrade them, take some extra money from them and bringing them on to the premium pages of back page, third page and the front page also.

items.statement: Circulation at ~38 lakh copies (37.68 lakh in Q2 vs ~38 lakh prior quarter); ~30,000 copies lost QoQ; focus on maintaining core market share, non-core markets less concerning
items.quote: We are at around 38 lakh copies. If you compare the last quarter, numbers are almost the same. So all efforts are there to make sure that we continue having the base, but a f ew percentage here and there is the one which is bothering us.

items.statement: Digital app subscription price hiked from INR149 to INR199 on experimental basis (cohort testing); too early to quantify revenue impact; advertising, subscription and tie-ups all nascent
items.quote: First of all, the price hike, which we have taken from INR149 to INR199, this will all be experimental basis. It's not a flat. Some places we have even tried slightly lesser, even monthly price and all that.

items.statement: Digital MAU declined from 20M (Q4) to 18M (Q2) due to reduced marketing spend and subscription experiments; QoQ decline ~3-4%
items.quote: We have tried to reduce the marketing spend on this entire activity because we believ e now brands should be able to sustain the readers' base based on th eir own merits and the organic. So we have reduced the marketing spend.

items.statement: UP election advertising uncertain but company has strong ground coverage, sizable MAU/downloads and journalist network in UP; hopeful subscriber base will grow during elections
items.quote: today we have got huge connect with the readers in UP. We have got very sizable downloads of our monthly active users as well as BAU. Also, we have got a huge network of our journalists in UP.

items.statement: No major capex planned for next 4-5 quarters; all machines and production equipment in place
items.quote: we don't have any large capex planned because all the machines, production e quipments and all are all in place. So we don't see -- foresee any major capex coming in a couple of quarters or maybe 4, 5 quarters ahead.

items.statement: Cash and bank balance ~INR1,120 crore; first interim dividend INR5/share paid in Q1; further distribution to be decided by Board
items.quote: As on today, company has a total cash and bank balance of around INR1,120 crores. And as you know, the company has already paid INR5 per share as the first interim dividend in the Q1.

items.statement: Other income INR13.39 crore from derecognition of ROU assets and lease liability due to termination of Ahmedabad registered office lease (builder redevelopment)
items.quote: lease agreement of Ahmedabad has been terminated because the builder from whom we have taken the premise, they are going for redevelopment. So we have derecognized the ROU assets and lease liabi lity, booked the gain of around INR13.39 crores under the head of other income as per the Ind AS 116/109 regulation.

items.statement: Hired senior executive for digital SBU head but experienced exit due to expectation-delivery mismatch; digital team working on multiple experiments
items.quote: We have hired a team. They are working hard on it. Unfortunately, there has been an exit also on that because there was an expectation and the delivery mismatch over there.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation a concern for newsprint costs and overall demand outlook; monsoon irregularities in Rajasthan may affect near-term advertising
items.quote: Especially I'm more concerned about the geopolitical situation. But having said that, looking at the overall momentum which our country has, I'm pretty optimistic on the next 2 quarters also.

items.statement: Radio Q2 revenue INR39 crore vs INR43 crore YoY; EBITDA INR11 crore vs INR13 crore; H1 revenue stable INR82 crore, EBITDA improved to INR26 crore from INR24 crore
items.quote: Revenue for Q2 FY27 stood at INR39 crores compared to INR43 crores in Q2 FY26, while EBITDA stood at INR11 crores against INR13 crores.

items.statement: Other expenses increased QoQ due to sales-based events (conclaves) where cost and revenue both booked; personnel and other costs under control; newsprint only uncontrolled cost
items.quote: Because if you compare, there's a reduction on this. But between Q1 and Q2, the increase because these are the sales-based events. So they generate revenue from a particular event and they also book it as a cost.

items.statement: Management aspires for high-teens revenue growth in FY27 and double-digit growth over the long term.
items.quote: Over the long term, we want to aspire for a double-digit growth. And yes, for the year, we are expecting a high teens, and that's what we've just said.

items.statement: Management does not provide quarterly guidance.
items.quote: So unfortunately, I can't guide you towards next quarter or thereon.

items.statement: Almond Drops Hair Oil delivered double-digit unit volume growth across pack groups and channels, led by small and medium packs.
items.quote: Almond Drops Hair Oil continues with its strong performance in this quarter and has delivered double -digit unit volume growth.

items.statement: Coconut franchise delivered strong volume growth across channels.
items.quote: As we move to the growth portfolio, the coconut franchise delivered a strong volume growth across channels.

items.statement: General trade and organized trade both grew in the strong mid-20s; rural grew marginally ahead of urban; quick commerce is the fastest-growing sub-channel.
items.quote: This quarter saw continued momentum in our general trade channel, which grew in line with organized trade, and both channels delivered growth in the strong mid-20s.

items.statement: International business grew ahead of company average in H1 except Bangladesh which grew in the teens due to tough environment.
items.quote: This channel for the full H1 has grown ahead of the company growth, and except for Bangladesh, most of our other ke y markets individually have also grown ahead of the company average.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 25%, PAT margin 21%; H1 EBITDA INR167 cr (85% growth), PAT INR141 cr (75% growth).
items.quote: On margins, we delivered an EBITDA of INR53 crores with an EBITDA margin of 25%, and a PAT of INR70 crores with a PAT margin of 21%.

items.statement: Gross margin 59.9% in Q2 and 60.8% in H1; sequential reduction offset by fixed and employee cost savings.
items.quote: Our gross margins for the quarter were at 59.9%, and overall for the first half of the year at 60.8%.

items.statement: Focus is on growing absolute EBITDA pool rather than percentage margin in inflationary environment.
items.quote: One, see, in an inflationary environment, our attempt is to protect and grow the absolute EBITDA pool rather than a percentage EBITDA pool.

items.statement: Calibrated price increase of ~5% in Q3 split roughly equally between 2-3% frontal price increase and similar contribution from ml-age reductions.
items.quote: In this round, we are approximately taking a 5% increase in consumer price, which will be split roughly equally between frontal price increase of 2% to 3% and a similar contribution coming through ml-age reductions.

items.statement: Endeavor to pass on absolute cost increases rather than protect percentage gross margin; peers also taking price hikes.
items.quote: And we are taking price increase which we believe would be sufficient to cover the kind of a cost impact we would need to manage our overall P&L.

items.statement: Key raw material prices volatile due to West Asia war, edible oil inflation, and cascading impact.
items.quote: On the overall margin front, this quarter witnessed continued volatility in key raw material prices due to the West Asia war, edible oil inflation, and the cascading impact of these two things.

items.statement: Relaunched and launched new SKUs in growth portfolio: refined amla oil proposition, upgraded body lotion product and packaging, Banjara's packs extending into large adjacent categories.
items.quote: In amla oils, we have refined the consumer proposition and are testing the new mix in general trade. In body lotion, we have upgraded both the product and packaging, and will test it on e-commerce. In Banjara's, we have introduced packs that extend the brand into large adjacent categories, which could offer significant growth potential for us if we are successful.

items.statement: Test marketing Banjara's lip balm and color shampoo (INR15) in four southern states to leverage herbal equity and expanded distribution.
items.quote: We are test marketing these in Banjara's markets core markets only, which are the four southern states. The belief which we have is Banjara's is a company which has been there in these markets for many decades, and hence, there is a very strong equity around the herbal, natural, you know, brand values which exist.

items.statement: Organized trade contributes close to 30% of company revenue; price point packs contribute less than 20% (in teens) of ADHO value sales.
items.quote: Contribution of organized trade channel in value terms to the overall company is close to 30%.

items.statement: Project Aarohan Phase 1 completed: added over 1 lakh outlets, 1,000+ distribution points, closed 600+ van routes across 13 states.
items.quote: We've been able to add over 1 lakh outlets, a 1,000-plus distribution points, and have been able to close over 600 van routes, achieving an expansion in direct reach and a reduction in fixed S&D cost.

items.statement: Aarohan 2.0 targets 10% expansion of direct reach in urban and more than 10% in rural over next six quarters across all 27 states.
items.quote: In Aarohan 2.0, we will focus all our energies on expansion of our direct reach in urban by 10%, and in rural -- by more than that over the next six quarters.

items.statement: Outsourced Guwahati factory production to third-party facility at start of FY27 for better operating efficiencies.
items.quote: So, see, what has happened is that we have outsourced basically the production of one of our factories in Guwahati from a company-owned facility to a third-party-run facility to drive better operating efficiencies towards the beginning of this financial year.

items.statement: International business profitability improved sharply on revenue scale-up, margin correction, and cost optimization.
items.quote: Our international business is also improving a sharp improvement in profitability. And on the back of revenue scale -up, margin correction, and cost optimization, we are delivering a good improvement in the EBITDA margins of this channel.

items.statement: Keeping inventory and procurement lean, buying only small quantities as costs believed to be at highest level.
items.quote: And what we are doing is that we are we are buying, we believe that the cost is at the highest level possible. And hence, our fresh buys are only for very, very small quantities. We are kind of keeping our inventory and our entire system very lean.

items.statement: No M&A deal stage or reportable update as of now.
items.quote: No, nothing to report as of now. We are not at any deal stage or we are not at any stage wherein we can report something.

items.statement: A&P spend up 7% YoY in Q2 and 18% in H1; optimized non-working A&P and reworked media operating cycles for spend efficiencies.
items.quote: Our consolidated A&P spend for the quarter were up 7% over the same period last year, and are up 18% on H1 basis. We continue to maintain robust SOV/SOM ratios in traditional and digital media, and we have carefully optimized the non -working A&P and reworked our media operating cycles to create some spend efficiencies.

items.statement: Biggest risk from changing consumer preferences impacts less than 1-1.5% of households; category has 91%+ penetration.
items.quote: This is a category of ours where we operate which has a 91% plus penetration, which means nearly every single household in the country uses this. The change in demographics or the change in preferences which possibly you're referring to is what we see impacting less than maybe 1% to 1.5% of the households in the country.

items.statement: Rural demand concerns (El Nino, harvest) are a while away; government easing measures underway; management remains optimistic.
items.quote: See, I think it's early, but we remain optimistic. At the same point of time, I would say it is early because, you know, whatever concerns which we are talking about which included you talked about in terms of rural demand, El Niño, they are all a while away.

items.statement: Unit volume growth reported as toughest measure; excludes free volume impact; ADHO unit volume growth double-digit.
items.quote: So, the reason why we've given and reported unit volume is because it does not take into account any free volume, any benefit on account of volumes going inside it. And hence, it is a reflection of how many bottles get sold or how many times the consumer has come and bought it.

items.statement: Quick commerce is demand fulfillment channel for large brands like Almond Drops; demand creation plus fulfillment for premium urban variants.
items.quote: So, for very large and very well-distributed brands like Almond Drops, the channel would be a demand fulfillment channel, you know, providing convenience to the consumer. But when it comes into more premium variants or more urban variants which are targeted at the urban elite, let's say, for example, serums or certain other higher-end personal care products, for those products, we will also look a

items.statement: AUM growth guidance of 30%-35% CAGR and profitability growth of 35%-40% CAGR
items.quote: Guidance, we will maintain 30% to 35% CAGR from the AUM perspective, and 35%-40% CAGR from profitability perspective.

items.statement: Target to reach INR10,000-11,000 crores AUM in 2-3 years
items.quote: Maybe 2 years to 3 years is the target for us to reach INR10,000 or INR11,000 kind of number.

items.statement: Digital lending to contribute ~10% of overall AUM in 2-3 years
items.quote: If I were to look at our journey of INR10,000 crores in next 2 to 3 years, I think digital lending should contribute around 10% to our overall AUM.

items.statement: Maintain ROA >4.5% and cost-to-income <15%
items.quote: We have also achieved all our key operating parameters: maintained nil NPA, return on assets is more than 4.5% and cost-to-income continues to remain less than 15% and we plan to maintain this in quarters to come as well.

items.statement: Supply chain to remain ~2/3 of AUM for next 2-3 years
items.quote: We would want to remain supply-chain-focused NBFC. Two-third of our AUM, at least in next 2 years to 3 years, we plan to be around supply chain only.

items.statement: Loan book at all-time high of ~INR5,700 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our loan book is also at an all-time high of around INR5,700 crores.

items.statement: Factoring contributes ~15% of loan book
items.quote: Around 15% contribution to our book is coming from the factoring.

items.statement: Digital lending book ~INR17 crores with 4 loans disbursed
items.quote: So far, we have di sbursed only four loan against property products with a book outstanding of INR17 crores

items.statement: Disbursed >INR16,000 crores in H1 FY27 (46% YoY growth)
items.quote: We continue to leverage our digital infrastructure and disbursed loans of more than INR16,000 crores in H1, which means volumes of INR32,000 crores on an annualized basis, which translates to less than 2 months of payback cycle for our loan book. This volume, if you were to compare on a year-on-year basis has gone up by 46%.

items.statement: Target 2 new anchor corporates per month for next 12-18 months
items.quote: The target in our mind is 2 anchors per month. That is the run rate we want to operate at least for the next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Yield maintained at ~13% (12.5% ROI + 50-70bps fee income)
items.quote: we're maintaining 13% kind of a yield. 12.5% odd as a ROI and around 50 basis point to 70 basis point as fee income, both put together, around 13% is the yield on our overall AUM whi ch we are

items.statement: Interest cost as % of income rose due to higher leverage (asset-to-equity 2.8x to 3.7x)
items.quote: Leverage. Our asset-to-equity has gone up from 2.8x to 3.7x in last two quarters. So when the leverage goes up, mathematically the interest cost will go up. But it translates to a better return on equity.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing ~8% from 19 bank/NBFC relationships
items.quote: Our cost of borrowing is around 8%. That is something unheard for NBFCs of our size and scale.

items.statement: 60+ DPD zero across entire book; 30+ DPD zero in non-supply chain
items.quote: On the overall book today, 60 DPD is zero, inclu ding supply chain and non -supply chain. In non-supply chain, 30 DPD is zero

items.statement: Accumulated provisions ~INR25 crores (regulatory ECL/IRAC, not cash credit cost)
items.quote: Today, we have accumulated maybe around INR25 crores kind of provisions in our balance sheet, which adds to our overall strength of the balance sheet, and that's the requirement of the regulator.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity leverage cap revised from 3x to 4x; board approved incremental borrowing
items.quote: Our mid-term target was to not leverage ourselves beyond debt-to-equity of 3x. But now considering the growth which has front-loaded, we are revising our leverage to debt-to-equity of 4x. Today in our board meeting also, board has approved the incremental borrowing, so we would like to leverage ourselves more.

items.statement: Borrowings solely from banks/NBFCs (19 relationships); small CP opportunistically
items.quote: of ban ks and NBFCs, and we leverage that relationship. Today, we have a relationship with 19 banks and NBFCs in the country. And all these 19 banks and NBFCs have given us financing either in form of working capital or term loans. Small bit , on opportunistic b asis, we do commercial paper also

items.statement: 15% strategic stake in AI/digital technology subsidiary for in-house stack
items.quote: We believe from a data security perspective, and from the dependency perspective, having an in-house AI digital stack is a better way forward. That's why we are beginning with a small 15% stake, which is more strategic and a long-term in nature.

items.statement: No equity raise planned this financial year; leverage increased to 4x instead
items.quote: No. Our mid-term target was to not leverage ourselves beyond debt-to-equity of 3x. But now considering the growth which has front-loaded, we are revising our leverage to debt-to-equity of 4x.

items.statement: Launched Factoring, TReDS, digital lending (BharatPe), and loan against property in Q2
items.quote: Apart from dealer financing and deep-tier financing, we have started doing Factoring and TReDS. We have also commercialized digital lending and loan against property during the quarter.

items.statement: Sector mix: ~35% steel/building products, ~20% auto, rest pharma, IT, tiles, electricals, cables
items.quote: If I were to dissect it, around 35% would be steel and building products, another 20% odd would be auto, and then there are varied industry, we are into pharma, IT, Tiles, Electricals, Cables, so on.

items.statement: Group ecosystem dependency reduced to 25% of book; powering 60+ anchor brands
items.quote: We continue to be a supply -chain-focused NBFC, supply cha in contributing to ~70% of our AUM today. This is despite reduction in our dependency on the group ’s ecosystem . The contribution of group’s ecosystem to our book has come down to 25% now. Currently, we are powering the ecosystem of more than 60 brands in the country

items.statement: Team doubled to 100+ in last year; per-employee PAT >INR2 crores annualized
items.quote: To augment business growth, we have almost doubled our team strength in last 1 year. Today, we have a strong team of more than 100 people. However, we continue to maint ain high productivity. On an annualized basis, our per-employee PAT is more than INR2 crores

items.statement: Aligned with RBI draft revolving credit guidelines; supply chain is term-based with no rollovers/extensions
items.quote: guidelines, we are ready because we are not doing anything which anyways is prohibited by RBI. Only thing which will happen, probably we will need to tweak certain documentation and the systems so that the reporting to the credit bureaus and the documentation with the client can become more digital and real-time instead of doing at a principle-level limit setups

items.statement: Digital lending NPA risk mitigated via FLDG, in-built cushions, anchor-led model
items.quote: NPA does happen. But philosophy of the group is very simple - nil NPAs. And that we want to maintain in BharatPe arrangement also. Maybe at a gross level, NPA may be there. But what matters whether NPAs are hurting us or not. So we have in-built cushions in form of better commercial or FLDG from LSPs.

items.statement: Payback cycle <2 months (annualized disbursement INR32,000 crores vs book INR5,700 crores)
items.quote: We continue to leverage our digital infrastructure and disbursed loans of more than INR16,000 crores in H1, which means volumes of INR32,000 crores on an annualized basis, which translates to less than 2 months of payback cycle for our loan book.

items.statement: No growth guidance provided; focus on sustainable VNB growth over medium term
items.quote: We don't provide guidance. We can give you what we should look at from the medium term.

items.statement: Retail protection growth expected to moderate from 40-50% to more moderate levels in H2 FY27
items.quote: The expectation is that as you get into H2 of this year, those growth numbers should taper down from the 40%-50% that we've been seeing to more moderate levels.

items.statement: VNB margin expanded 130 bps to 26.0% in H1 FY27 driven by product mix shift toward protection
items.quote: VNB margin stood at 26.0%, an expansion of 130 basis points from the full-year margin of 24.7% last year.

items.statement: VNB grew 22.3% YoY to ₹12.83 billion in H1 FY27; total premium grew 15.3% to ₹245.05 billion
items.quote: VNB growing by 22.3% to ₹ 12.83 billion in H1 -FY2027, and margins stood at 26.0%. Total premium grew by 15.3% year-on-year to ₹ 245.05 billion.

items.statement: Sum assured grew 30.1% YoY to ₹8.81 trillion; retail sum assured up 34.9% to ₹2.32 trillion
items.quote: In H1-FY2027, our sum assured grew by 30.1% to ₹ 8.81 trillion, supported by a strong 39.5% year-on-year growth in protection APE.

items.statement: Protection mix increased to 23.4% of APE from 19.3%; savings mix moderated to 76.6% from 80.7%
items.quote: The overall protection mix increased from 19.3% in H1 -FY2026 to 23.4% of APE in H1 -FY2027. Consequently, the savings business mix moderated from 80.7% in H1 -FY2026 to 76.6% in H1-FY2027.

items.statement: 2.41 lakh+ advisors, 52 bank partnerships with 27,000+ branches, 1,600+ non-bank partnerships
items.quote: Today, we have the strength of 2.41 lakh + advisors, 52 bank partnerships with access to more than 27,000 bank branches, and 1,600+ non-bank partnerships.

items.statement: Cost to Premium ratio ex-GST reduced 30 bps to 18.3%; Savings Cost to Premium ex-GST reduced 90 bps to 11.6%
items.quote: Our Cost to Premium ratio, excluding GST, reduced by 30 basis points year -on-year to 18.3% in H1-FY2027, and the Savings Cost to Premium ratio, excluding GST, reduced by 90 basis points year-on-year to 11.6% over the same period.

items.statement: Operating expenses ex-GST and stamp duty reduced at 8% CAGR over 3 years; 22% absolute reduction in FY26 vs FY23
items.quote: Our operating expenses, excluding GST and stamp duty, have reduced at a CAGR of 8% over the last three years, an absolute 22% reduction in FY2026 compared to FY2023.

items.statement: IRDAI consultation paper on distribution economics proposes recalibrated expense limits and differentiated commission caps; feedback due end of month
items.quote: IRDAI has released a public consultation paper on recalibrating economics of insurance distribution. This paper lays the groundwork for greater efficiency, fostering healthy competition and enhanced transparency across the insurance sector.

items.statement: Credit life commission cuts proposed but product serves critical societal need for low-income groups; regulator will consider feedback
items.quote: See, credit life is, as a protection product, it provides a very important societal need in a country. It alleviates the stress of any asset repossession in case of any untimely death of the breadwinner.

items.statement: Claim settlement ratio 99.3% with 1.1 day TAT for non-investigated claims; early claim ratio 23% best-in-class; zero NPAs since inception
items.quote: Our claim settlement ratio remained industry -leading at 99.3% in H1-FY2027, with an average turnaround time of 1.1 days for non -investigated claims. Our early claim ratio stood at 23%, which is the best -in-class in the industry.

items.statement: Embedded value grew 12.2% YoY to ₹566.69 billion; value of in-force business grew 12% to ₹423.89 billion
items.quote: Our embedded value grew by 12.2% year-on-year to ₹ 566.69 billion at September 30th, 2026. Within the EV, the value of in -force business grew by 12% year -on-year to ₹ 423.89 billion.

items.statement: Profit after tax grew 26.5% YoY to ₹7.60 billion in H1 FY27
items.quote: Profit after tax grew by 26.5% year-on-year to ₹ 7.60 billion in H1-FY2027.

items.statement: Sidharatha Mishra appointed MD & CEO for 5 years from Oct 14, 2026; assumed COO role from Oct 6, 2026
items.quote: As you are aware, the Board has appointed Sidharatha as the MD and CEO of ICICI Life for a tenure of 5 years, beginning October 14, 2026, subject to the requisite approvals. He has already assumed the role of COO from October 6, 2026.

items.statement: New CEO strategy unchanged: sustainable VNB growth balancing growth, profitability, risk; protection and annuity central
items.quote: Our strategy remains unchanged, delivering sustainable VNB growth while balancing business growth, profitability, and risk and prudence. Protection and annuity stay central to our strategy.

items.statement: 54% of savings policies issued same day reflecting straight-through processing and automation progress
items.quote: In H1-FY2027, 54% of our savings policies were issued on the same day, reflecting the progress we have made in straight -through processing and automation.

items.statement: Non-par and annuity products attractive across all channels; competitive intensity managed through IRR offerings and opex efficiency
items.quote: These products are very attractive in terms of IRRs, both the annuities, which have been on the regular pay variety, as well as the guaranteed products, which also are both income as well as lump sum variety. And they've done quite well across all of our distribution channels.

items.statement: Sum of variances positive; economic variance close to zero in H1 FY27 EV walk
items.quote: So, Nidhesh, we've not broken the entire walk at this point, but I think the sum total of variances is positive. Economic variance is very close to zero.

items.statement: Company renamed to ICICI Life Insurance Limited strengthening brand identity with ICICI Group
items.quote: The company has been renamed “ICICI Life Insurance Limited”, strengthening our identity with brand ICICI, that millions of Indians associate with trust, strength, and easy access to financial services.

items.statement: Quarterly average AUM was INR9.69 trillion, up 10% year-on-year and 4% sequentially.
items.quote: Our quarterly average AUM stood at INR9.69 trillion, up 10% year -on-year and 4% sequentially.

items.statement: Equity-oriented assets stood at INR6.51 trillion, representing 67.1% of AUM versus 57.5% for the industry.
items.quote: Equity -oriented asset s stood at INR6.51 trillion, representing 67.1% of our AUM compared with 57.5% for the industry.

items.statement: Actively managed equity AUM grew 14% year-on-year to INR6.08 trillion with 12.7% market share.
items.quote: Within this, actively managed equity AUM grew by 14% year -on-year to INR6.08 trillion with a market share of 12.7%.

items.statement: Debt AUM stood at INR1.62 trillion with 13% market share; liquid AUM grew 10% year-on-year to INR860 billion.
items.quote: On fixed income, debt AUM stood at INR1.62 trillion with a 13% market share, while liquid AUM grew 10% year-on-year to INR860 billion.

items.statement: Live individual accounts increased to 32 million from 26 million a year ago; unique investor base at 17.7 million with 28% penetration.
items.quote: Our live individual accounts increased to 32 mill ion from 26 million a year ago. Our unique investor base stood at 17.7 million, representing a penetration of 28%.

items.statement: Systematic flows (SIPs and STPs) were INR48 billion in September, up 6% year-on-year across 19 million transactions.
items.quote: Our systematic flows comprising of SIPs and STPs, that is s ystematic transfer plans, stood at INR48 billion in September, up 6% year-on-year across 19 million transactions.

items.statement: Launched two new AIFs: a Category II equity fund focused on private markets and a Category III fund investing in listed securities.
items.quote: During the quarter, we also launched 2 new AIFs, a Category II equity fund focused on private markets. We are anticipating first close in thi s quarter and also launched the Category III fund, investing in listed securities, which achieved first close during the last quarter.

items.statement: Started managing EPFO fixed income mandate during the quarter.
items.quote: We have started managing EPFO fixed income mandate during the quarter that went by.

items.statement: Revenue from operations was INR11.7 billion, up 14% year-on-year; operating profit INR9.1 billion, up 16% with operating margin of 36 basis points of AUM.
items.quote: Revenue from operations for the quarter was INR11.7 billion, up 14% year-on-year. Operating profit was INR9.1 billion, up 16% with an operating margin of 36 basis points of AUM.

items.statement: Active equity yield 61 bps, overall equity 58 bps, debt 28-29 bps, liquid 13 bps for the quarter.
items.quote: So, for active equity, our yield were 61 basis points. For overall equity fund, this was 58 basis points. Debt is around 28, 29 basis points. Liquid, 13 basis points.

items.statement: Sequential yield improvement largely due to asset mix change, not material movement.
items.quote: Largely asset mix change. It's not like a material movement. It's slightly upwards from previous quarter.

items.statement: AIF fees sit at 80-90 bps, above mutual fund equity book; discretionary PMS earns broadly same as equity MF; non-discretionary PMS is strategic; government mandates priced competitively.
items.quote: On the margins question, AIF is a margin-accretive business. Fees here sit above what we earn on our mutual fund equity book in the range of 80 to 90 basis points depending on the product.

items.statement: SIP share growing; confident on SIP book despite competition from newer AMCs with track records.
items.quote: And we remain confident. I think this is one of the biggest area of focus for us and remain very confident on our SIP book.

items.statement: Systematic transactions rose from 17 million in June to nearly 19 million in September; monthly systematic book grown nearly 5x in 5 years to INR48 billion vs industry 3x.
items.quote: So our systematic transactions rose from about 17 million in June to nearly 19 million in September. And if we step back for a moment, monthly systematic transaction book has grown nearly 5x in about 5 years to around INR48 billion and industry in the same p eriod would have grown 3x.

items.statement: Investing in alternatives platform with over 20 investment professionals; expanding investor servicing, operations, sales, distribution; investing in international, digital, technology, AI-led capabilities.
items.quote: So between alternative and PMS, when I say alternative, both private equity and private credit, we've got more than 20 investment professionals now and significantly expanding our capacity on investor servicing, on operations, on the whole sales and then the distribution side, so on and so forth.

items.statement: Mutual fund investment team grown from ~30 to ~40 professionals; will continue to grow as AUM scales to INR20-40 lakh crores.
items.quote: But even on the mutual fund side, team till a couple of years back was like 30 professionals. Now number is like closer to 40, and this will continue to grow.

items.statement: ESOP non-cash expense for Q2 FY27 was INR186 million (INR18.6 crores); full year FY27 expected around INR79-80 crores.
items.quote: So for this quarter, it's already disclosed, it's about INR186 million for the quarter. So INR18.6 crores. Yes, it's alre ady, as a footnote on Page 27.

items.statement: SIF platform ready with two senior hires (Ihab Dalwai, Paul Parampreet Singh); expect couple of product launches over next couple of quarters.
items.quote: We've got Ihab Dalwai and Paul Parampreet Singh. We are now well set, and you will see a couple of product launches in this space over the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Passive portfolio has almost 50 products across market cap indices, smart beta, sector/thematic, index funds, ETFs, fund of funds; index fund market share very high, second highest in retail.
items.quote: So we have almost 50 products on the passive side across market cap -based indices and smart beta, across plain vani lla indexes versus sector thematic, and across index fund, and ETFs and of course, some of the fund of funds, which feed into these ETFs.

items.statement: One-stop platform across active, passive, PMS (discretionary and non-discretionary), AIFs (fund of fund, private equity, private credit), International (6 inbound, 2 outbound funds).
items.quote: On the other side, non-mutual funds, we have got a fairly wide bouquet of products on PMS, both discretionary and nondiscretionary. On the Alternative side, we've got a fund of fund. We have got now a new private equity venture fund and a private credit fund and then, of course, on the International side, we have just concluded the NFO of two outbound funds, and we have got a 6 inbound funds.

items.statement: Indian retail investors showing resilience and discipline; SIP flows grown from INR30 billion to INR325 billion monthly over 10 years; large part of equity/hybrid net flows now via SIPs giving predictability.
items.quote: And you can clearly see in the SIP flows over the last several years. 10 years back, the monthly flow used to be 30 billion, and now we are talking about 325 billion. So there has been a consistent increase during this period.

items.statement: Mid-cap fund AUM over INR1 lakh crore (20th year); small-cap fund at INR40,000 crores but still 0.5% of small-cap universe market cap; weighted average market cap below category average.
items.quote: In fact, it's our 20th year of the mid -cap fund. It's more than INR1 lakh crore. And I think we take deep pride in what we have delivered over the last two decades.

items.statement: Newer players validate industry growth potential; HDFC AMC has comprehensive platform, deep relationships, well-developed distribution network; confident of capturing financialization of savings opportunity.
items.quote: No, I think that the entry of newer players only validates our thesis that industry has a huge growth potential. And I mean, for us, it is not appropriate to comment on any particular name or firm, but we have a comprehensive platform across active, passive, alternatives. We are continuously expanding , building deep relationship s and extremely well-developed distribution network.

items.statement: Board distributed almost entire post-tax cash profits as dividend last year; balance sheet cash used for seed capital for alternate platforms; investment schedule disclosed in investor pack.
items.quote: For the last year, the Board ha s declared a dividend, which effectively where we have distributed the almost entire post-tax cash profits that we generate. The balance sheet that we have, currently, we are using for seed capital for all our alternate platforms.

items.statement: GIFT City subsidiary: 6 inbound funds for global investors, recently launched 2 outbound funds (developed market feeder, emerging market feeder); will keep evaluating and growing strategies.
items.quote: We have got six funds for inbound investment that is investment by global investors in India. And recently, we have launched two products for outbound where there's an opportunity for Indian investors to invest globally.

items.statement: Blended equity yield at 58 bps vs some peers at 67 bps due to large fund sizes triggering SEBI TER reduction formula; three funds above INR1 lakh crore AUM.
items.quote: So some of our funds are large in size. They have grown very well. So we are the only asset management company which today has three funds, well above the 1 lakh crores in terms of AUM. As you know, right? The SEBI formula, as the AUM grows larger, the TER keep coming down.

items.statement: No guidance on when alternate business will reach INR100 crores revenue; focus on building full-stack platform across mutual funds, PMS, AIF.
items.quote: Devesh, we don't give guidance like this when will we reach a certain amount. All I can say is that beyond mutual funds, now the alternative platform is working as a full stack.

items.statement: No future guidance on equity yield targets; will optimize franchise to fullest.
items.quote: Sir, we don't hazard a guess on anything that is in future. I think we have been able to build a strong franchise over time. We'll obviously do our best to optimize it to the fullest.

items.statement: H1 cost numbers skewed by CSR expenses taken in Q1; requested to view total cost on annual basis for trend.
items.quote: Sir, actually, we had mentioned this in our last quarterly call. There were some CSR expenses which were taken up in the first quarter. And because of that, you are seeing the H1 numbers getting kind of a bit skewed.

items.statement: Cost-to-operating-income ratio improvement of 100-150 bps year-on-year guided
items.quote: I think we had guided for a 1 - 1.5% kind of overall improvement year-on-year. I think we are well on course to achieve that.

items.statement: UBS collaboration targets $600-650 million flows for current financial year
items.quote: So, in some senses, we've internally looked at a target of exchanging $600 odd million in flows for the current financial year.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target of 46-47% over next 12-18 months
items.quote: And as we build out our teams across all our businesses, we continue to hope that we'll make it more and more efficient and try and move that 48 towards the 46 - 47 number.

items.statement: Total AUM at ₹9 lakh crores, up 31% YoY; ARR AUM at ₹3,53,000 crores, up 19.7% YoY
items.quote: Total AUMs stood at about ₹9 lakh crores, up 31% year-on-year. ARR AUMs stood at ₹3,53,000 crores, up 19.7% year-on-year.

items.statement: ARR net flows of ₹12,482 crores in Q2 vs ₹10,815 crores in Q1
items.quote: ARR net flows of ₹12,482 crores during the quarter, compared to ₹10,815 crores in Q1.

items.statement: 360 ONE Plus advisory platform crossed ₹1 lakh crores AUM
items.quote: 360 ONE Plus, our advisory platform, has now crossed ₹1 lakh crores.

items.statement: HNI business manages over ₹8,000 crores for 1,500+ clients with 60 RMs
items.quote: It now manages over ₹8,000 crores at healthy retentions for over 1,500 clients and about 60 relationship managers.

items.statement: ET Money distribution segment ARR AUM over ₹700 crores in last nine months
items.quote: The distribution segment of the business clocked ARR AUM of over ₹700 crores over the last nine 3 months

items.statement: Asset management ARR AUM over ₹1,00,000 crores, up 9.4% YoY; net flows ₹1,492 crores
items.quote: In the asset management segment, ARR AUM stood at a little over ₹100,000 crores, up 9.4% year-on-year. Net flows improved to ₹1,492 crores after the large SMA redemptions in Q1.

items.statement: Dyna-SIF AUM crossed ₹1,000 crores; won first European institutional mandate and top-up from existing global mandate
items.quote: Our SIF strategy has gained traction with Dyna-SIF AUM crossing ₹1,000 crores. We won our first European institutional mandate and received a top-up from an existing global mandate.

items.statement: ARR revenue grew 27.5% YoY to ₹706 crores; ARR retention improved to 79 bps from 74 bps in Q1
items.quote: ARR revenue grew 27.5% y-o-y to ₹706 crores. ARR now contributes 79% of operating revenues, and ARR retention improved to 79 basis points from 74 basis points in Q1.

items.statement: Wealth ARR revenue grew 40.5% YoY to ₹503 crores; retention improved to 79 bps from 71 bps
items.quote: ARR revenue grew 40.5% year-on-year to ₹503 crores. Retention improved to 79 basis points from 71 basis points in Q1.

items.statement: Asset management ARR revenue ₹203 crores with 79 bps retention; operating PBT ₹108 crores
items.quote: ARR revenue was ₹203 crores with retentions of 79 basis points, and operating PBT was ₹108 crores.

items.statement: Cost-to-operating-income ratio improved to 51.5% from 54.3% in Q1
items.quote: Our cost-to-operating income ratio improved to 51.5% from ₹54.3 in Q1.

items.statement: Carried interest from third-party funds contributed ~₹60 crores in Q2
items.quote: During Q2, carried interest from third-party funds contributed approximately ₹60 crores.

items.statement: UBS collaboration flows expected at 40-50 bps retention
items.quote: I think it's safe to assume 40 - 50 basis points of retention would broadly come through.

items.statement: UHNI segment growing at 13-15%; record IPO and monetization activity driving liquidity events
items.quote: The UHNI segment continues to grow at 13 - 15%, and monetization events such as IPOs, block deals, stake sales, keep releasing liquidity to promoters and families.

items.statement: Monthly SIP flows hit record ₹32,500 crores in September; 70 companies raised ₹90,500 crores via IPOs in Q2
items.quote: Monthly SIP flows touched a record of ₹32,500 crores in September, and close to 70 companies raised ₹90,500 crores through IPOs during the quarter.

items.statement: Clients with >₹10 crores AUM exceed 4,100, accounting for 95% of ex-custody wealth AUM
items.quote: Clients with more than ₹10 crores of AUM are over ₹4,100 and account for 95% of our ex-custody wealth AUM.

items.statement: New client additions: ~1/3 of net flows from new clients, 2/3 from existing; client base grew from 1,800-1,900 to ~4,200 families in 5 years
items.quote: I think we've steadily grown that number from 18 - 1,900, five years back, to around 4,200 families today.

items.statement: Client attrition <0.5% on count and <0.25% on AUM; 60-65% AUM from 5+ year vintage clients
items.quote: If you see last quarter, the attrition, less than half percent attrition of clients and even so less than quarter percent attrition on the AUM side.

items.statement: Margins stable post 2021-22 reset; differentiation via people-product-platform moat, not pricing
items.quote: I think the big reduction or big kind of reset in margins happened in 2021-22. I think it stayed there. And I don't really see that changing dramatically.

items.statement: 50% of Q2 flows from wallet share enhancement, 50% from new mandates (vs typical 70/30)
items.quote: We are quite excited about the fact that 50% of the flows actually came from enhancement of wallet share, and 50% actually come from new mandates.

items.statement: ET Money Advisory/ARR/MF regular AUM at ₹3,300-3,400 crores; HNI AUM ~₹8,800 crores including ₹2,000 crores transferred from UHNI
items.quote: ET Money are overall Advisory/ARR/Mutual fund and regular codes moved to around about ₹3,300 - 3,400 crores of ARR AUM.

items.statement: COMPASS AI layer live across wealth, asset management, enterprise; aims for efficiency, commercial impact, quality, control
items.quote: COMPASS, our proprietary and governed AI layer, is live across wealth, asset management, and enterprise functions.

items.statement: Ashish Agarwal joins senior leadership; 3 top-quartile hires including Ashish to strengthen leadership bench
items.quote: Ashish obviously joins in a senior leadership role and, along with me, will be kind of spearheading the business.

items.statement: Tangible ROE 16.9% in Q2; target ~20% over 3.5 years by doubling profits; UBS warrant conversion ~₹1,600 crores expected
items.quote: Tangible ROE stood at 16.9%.

items.statement: Equity brokerage revenue from UHNI/HNI clients rose from ₹4-5 crores/month to ₹8-9 crores/month post B&K acquisition; target ₹15-20 crores/month
items.quote: We've been able to pick up to close to around about ₹8 - 9 crores a month. So, I think that's something which I feel we've kind of under-delivered on for so many years.

items.statement: Stand-alone operating margin guidance of around 45% on annual basis for broking and distribution business
items.quote: we remain confident in our ability to sustain stand-alone operating margins of around 45% on an annual basis

items.statement: Employee cost guidance of about ₹1,100 crores including ESOP cost for FY27, flat year-on-year
items.quote: we'll continue to maintain our guidance of about ₹ 1,100 crores of employee costs, including the cost of stock options for this financial year, which is flat for year -on-year comparison

items.statement: Stand-alone operating margin reached 48.9% in Q2 FY27, exceeding guided range of 40-45%
items.quote: At the stand-alone level, operating margins reached 48.9%, exceeding our guided range of 40% to 45%.

items.statement: Consolidated operating margin expanded to 45.1% in Q2 FY27 from 34.5% a year ago
items.quote: Consolidated operating margins stood at 45.1% compared to 34.5% in the corresponding quarter last year, an expansion of over 1,000 basis points.

items.statement: Normalized consolidated operating margin stable at 43.8% in Q2 FY27 vs 43.6% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: after normalizing for seasonal IPL expenditure and ESOP -related reversals, consolidated operating margins remained stable at 43.8% compared to 43.6% in the preceding quarter

items.statement: Average client funding book reached lifetime high of ₹74.5 billion, up 40.5% year-on-year
items.quote: Our average client funding book reached a lifetime high of ₹ 74.5 billion, up about 40.5% from a year ago.

items.statement: Closing client funding book reached record ₹82.1 billion, funded clients increased nearly 30% to 437,000
items.quote: The average client funding book increased over 40% year -on-year to ₹ 74.5 billion, while the closing book reached a record ₹ 82.1 billion. Importantly, the number of funded clients increased by nearly 30% over the last year to 437,000

items.statement: Ionic Wealth AUM at ₹160 billion, up 19.1% over Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our wealth business is gaining depth as well with Ionic Wealth AUM at ₹ 160 billion, up 19.1% over Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Asset Management AUM stands at nearly ₹6 billion, evaluating comprehensive play including new leader
items.quote: In Asset Management, our AUM stands at nearly ₹ 6 billion, and we are evaluating a comprehensive play in this business, including bringing a new leader to build, scale, build and scale.

items.statement: Average daily orders rebounded to 5.8 million in September, up nearly 12% from August
items.quote: In September, average daily orders rebounded to 5.8 million, up nearly 12% from August.

items.statement: Added nearly 1.5 million new clients in Q2 FY27, 11.6% more than Q1
items.quote: We welcomed nearly 1.5 million new clients this quarter, 11.6% more than Q1

items.statement: NSE active client base grew, leading to expansion in active clients market share month-over-month each month of quarter
items.quote: We also witnessed growth in our NSE active client base, leading to an expansion in our active clients market shar e month-over-month in each month of this quarter.

items.statement: Equity retail market share based on option premium turnover at 19.7%, derivatives retail turnover share at 22.1% for quarter, rose to 22.5% in September
items.quote: Our overall equity retail market share based on option premium turnover stood at 19.7%. In the derivatives, we held our position with a retail turnover share of 22.1% for the quarter, and it rose to 22.5% in September

items.statement: Commodities turnover more than doubled year-on-year, market share at 44% due to market expansion
items.quote: In commodities, our turnover more than doubled over last year. Our share came down to 44% because of market expansion owing to more participants entering the market

items.statement: SIP registrations grew nearly 12% over Q1 FY27
items.quote: On investing, our SIP registrations grew nearly 12% over Q1.

items.statement: Credit distribution annualized run rate reached ₹33 billion in September, highest ever
items.quote: In September, we delivered our highest ever credit distribution, taking our annualized run rate to ₹ 33 billion.

items.statement: Gross broking income now ~55% of total revenues vs ~60% a year ago; interest income grew 34% YoY to ₹5.1 billion
items.quote: Gross broking income now accounts for approximately 55% of total revenues compared with nearly 60% a year ago. Interest income grew 34% year -on-year and 9% sequentially to ₹ 5.1 billion

items.statement: Distribution income growing healthily, ~5% of revenue in Q2, targeting low double digits in 2-3 years
items.quote: overall, if you see what is very interesting, which we've talked about in the long term is that beyond broking, you're going to see low double digits in the next 2 to 3 years, we're already starting to get to about 5% there in distribution revenue

items.statement: MTF lending rate maintained at 14.99% despite marginal increase in borrowing cost; NIMs not impacted
items.quote: I think for the time being, we are not looking at any increase in the lending cost. So it remains at 14.99%. And the cost of borrowing has marginally gone up be cause of the increase in the benchmark rate by RBI, but it's within our toleration limit. So it's okay. I mean, the NIMs haven't really gotten impacted.

items.statement: MTF portfolio granular and well-collateralized: 84% of funded clients have exposures below ₹100,000, 82% of book less than 30 days old, delinquencies negligible
items.quote: Approximately 84% of clients -- funded clients have exposures below ₹ 100,000, while 82% of the closing book is less than 30 days old. Classified as Internal Delinquencies remain negligible, reflecting the quality of the portfolio and our robust risk management

items.statement: MTF book quality solid with ability to square off if margins fall; book growing healthily
items.quote: the quality of the book is solid because our margins change depending on the scrip that we are giving MTF on. And therefore, a little to no risk on that front because we have the ability to square off if margins fall below a certain point. And I'm continuing to see that book grow in a very healthy way.

items.statement: IRDAI consultation paper proposes reset of insurance commissions to lower costs, favoring digital platforms like Angel One
items.quote: IRDAI's September consultation paper proposes a reset of insurance commissions with the aim to lower insurance costs, thus bringing the product within reach of many more Indians. It's still a proposal, but we believe a lower cost, more transparent model is good for the consumers and favors digital platforms like ours

items.statement: SEBI Board approved new portfolio manager regulations, enabling wider product shelf for platforms
items.quote: The regulatory backdrop is also turning positive supportive with SEBI's Board approving new portfolio manager regulations. A wider product shelf means platforms like ours can offer clients richer, more diversified portfolios.

items.statement: Received authorization to operate as Global Access Provider in IFSC; piloting U.S. stocks on platform with U.S. brokerage partner
items.quote: we have received authorization to operate as a Global Access Provider in the IFSC. With that, we are piloting U.S. stocks on our platform. We are excited about providing a simple way for our users to access the largest market in the world.

items.statement: Board approved second interim dividend of ₹1.4 per share for FY27 with record date October 22, 2026
items.quote: The Board has also approved the second interim dividend for this financial year of ₹ 1.4 per share with October 22, 2026, as the record date.

items.statement: Employee count ~3,050 as of September 30, down due to attrition in Q4/Q1; slowed backfills; focus on talent density over headcount
items.quote: the current employee count as of 30th September is close to about 3,050-odd employees. And yes, this has definitely come down. as Ambarish had mentioned that there were some attritions in quarter 4 and quarter 1. So that is there. We've slowed down the backfills

items.statement: MTF book classification: good and blue chip stocks constitute upwards of 85% of portfolio
items.quote: Largely, our book is good and blue chip constitutes almost upwards of 85%.

items.statement: Mutual fund distribution: regular plans about one-third of total distribution
items.quote: On MF distribution, regular is about one-third of the total distribution, if you look at it.

items.statement: F&O market share strong and rising (22.5% in September); not looking to change pricing; trusted player advantage limits price elasticity risk
items.quote: On F&O as you see our share actually is very strong and going up, if anything. So I don't think we are -- we think we have the right pricing right now. We are not looking to either increase or reduce it. At this time, I think it is working really, really well.

items.statement: Brand spend as percentage of revenue expected to decline over time as revenue scales while spend stays flat
items.quote: You should expect that over a period of time as a percentage of revenue, definitely, the spends will come down unless we sort of see a new opportunity, which in my mind, as a percentage of revenue, it will come down because I don't see the spend going up too much from here, but our revenue will scale.

name: Anand Rathi Share And Stock Brokers Ltd

items.statement: Targets MTF book of INR1,750-1,800 crores by end FY27 and ~40% growth in distribution AUM by end FY27
items.value: MTF INR1,750-1,800 cr; Distribution AUM growth ~40%
items.quote: We continue to target margin trading book size for approximately INR1,750 crores to INR1,800 crores by the year financial year '27. And there is going to be a growth of about 40% in AUM of our distribution business by the end of the current financial year.

items.statement: Targets 15-20% top-line growth and 20-30% bottom-line growth
