And we are working towards it, and I'm sure the whole team of Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers Limited is committed that the growth of about 15% to 20% on top line and about 20 to 25% to 30% on that bottom line.

items.statement: Distribution AUM grew 29% YoY to INR99,990 million
items.quote: Assets under management, which has increased by almost 29% year -on-year. Our Asset Management has grown by 29% to 99,990 million, while under custody grew by almost 13% year-on-year, to almost 1.15 trillion.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 PAT margin 15%; H1 FY27 PAT before exceptional items up 60% YoY
items.quote: PAT grew 50% year-on-year to 419 million, in quarter 2 of '27 with a margin of 15%. For first half PAT before exceptional items increased 60% year-on-year to 810 million, while profit after tax after exceptional items, it stood at 653 million, representing growth of 29% year-on-year.

items.statement: MTF NIM ~4.5%; borrowing cost ~9.5%
items.quote: In terms of our borrowings borrowing cost, it's there around 9.5%. And the positive part, even after this, like I have mentioned that because of the RBI circular, almost INR300 crores related impact was there to the company, then also we were able to main tain our cost at this kind of level. And gradually, we are further reducing that particular cost. In terms of NIM side, we are able to generate

items.statement: Equity cash volumes growing consistently; derivative volumes static or lower; company outperformed industry on F&O volumes
items.quote: So far equity market, cash market -related volumes are concerned, you see there is a constant, consistent growth. So far derivative capital market -related volume, if you really see, they are static or lower than earlier times. Obviously, our company is more tuned towards cash market volumes. And as and when these cash market volumes are better and we're doing good, our broking revenues are also i

items.statement: Targets broking growth 15-20% and non-broking growth 30-40% over next 2-3 years
items.quote: And as we have said, that we are going to grow our broking business by about 15% to 20%, and we are going to grow by about 30% to 35% and, in certain cases, 40% in our non -broking segment side. That's what our broader understanding and the broader criteria which we have set for ourselves, and we are working towards it.

items.statement: Total clients ~10.5 lakh; 55% associated >3 years; 71% active clients in Tier 2/3 cities
items.quote: Total clients increased to approximately 10.5 lakhs, as of September '26. Around 55% of our clients have been associated with us for more than 3 years, reflecting the strength of our relationships and the trust report in the Anand Rathi brand. Additionally , 71% of our active clients are located across Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities providing us with a broad and diversified franchise.

items.statement: MTF book NPA zero for 8 years; average book size per customer below INR17 lakh
items.quote: Considering all those facts, our NPA into MTF book is zero. We have started this activity 8 years back, and so far in last 8 years, we are able to maintain it at zero, and we will able to continue the manage the risk related to this MTF book.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio 1.02 as of Sep 30, 2026; disciplined leverage maintained
items.quote: Our debt equity ratio stood at 1.02, as of September 30 '26, and we continue to maintain disciplined leverage and adequate liquidity as we scale our MTF and other growth initiatives.

items.statement: Net cash position declined from ~INR2,700 cr to ~INR900 cr due to HNI clients converting cash margins to G-Secs; business intact
items.quote: Those clients who are keeping their margins in cash format with us for creating a bank guarantee or giving them limits, they withdrew the money. They converted that cash money into a government security and provided security margin to us. Obviously, that cash outflow has happened, and still we are managing, maintaining the, you know, customer's margin in by way of government securities, right?

items.statement: Employee expenses up 31% YoY due to insourcing of ~150 outsourced staff and RM/product team expansion; salary impact largely one-time
items.quote: So, there are two things which are happening. One side, naturally we are expanding our RM base on continuous basis at one side. Second side, we are strengthening our product team also because we keep on adding the multiple products. But one important chang e which took place in last quarter where few of the employees where the services were obtained from the outsourcing, those employees also we ha

items.statement: SEBI increased ARN transfer cooling period from 6 to 12 months, partially reducing mutual fund trail commission
items.quote: In mutual fund side, actually the regulator has changed the rule in last financial year, where earlier for any ARN transfer, transfer of the mutual fund from any other distributor, the income credit was not available for 6 months earli er, and rule has got changed. Now the cooling period is 12 months.

items.statement: Rising interest rates globally and domestically may pressure debt yields; equity preferred for long-term returns
items.quote: But number two, having said that, in terms of market scenario, since interest rates are on a rising trend, markets are uncertain and overall global scenarios suggest that in future also, due to inflammation pressure, I think interest rates are further goi ng to strengthen. Probably you may see the certain interest rate hike scenario globally as well as probably as it is in our country also.

items.statement: Investing in technology and digital capability; digital platform contributed 36% of brokerage income in H1 FY27
items.quote: Our investment in technology and digital capability continued to deliver a strong outcome. Digital platform contributed 36% of brokerage income in first half of '27 reflecting continuous focus on building a seamless scalable digital ecosystem.

items.statement: Outperformed industry on F&O volumes due to no proprietary trading; RBI circular reduced proprietary broking house volumes
items.quote: On F&O side, at exchange level, the volume's fall was comparatively higher because of the changes in RBI's circular towards the capital market exposure, many proprietary broking houses' volumes got reduced . But overall, since we don't have any proprietary -related volumes, we were able to actually improve in terms of our total volume versus the exchange , on the F&O side also, other than the cash

items.statement: Management expects to achieve the upper end of FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR 2,200-2,400 crores based on H1 performance
items.quote: I think considering the first two quarters of half -yearly projection that we have of INR1,100 crores, we can definitely achieve the upper part of the guidance.

items.statement: 6 GW integrated TOPCon cell and module expansion capex is INR 5,500 crores including INR 4,600 crores hard cost and INR 700 crores for working capital margin money and IDC
items.quote: So, Apoorva ji, that INR5,500 crores are for both cell and module of 6 gigawatt each. And it includes, where the hard cost is around INR 4,600 crores and the remaining cost is for your interest during construction, contingency, margin money for working capital for soft costs

items.statement: Module manufacturing facility expected to commission by December 2026, cell manufacturing facility by March 2027; total capacity will reach 16.3 GW modules and 8.9 GW cells
items.quote: We expect the commissioning of the module manufacturing facility by December, followed by cell manufacturing facility by March 20 27. Upon completion, our total installed manufacturing capacity will increase to approximately 16.3 gigawatt of modules and 8.9 gigawatt of cells.

items.statement: Order book at 10.4 GW as of September 30, 2026 with 1.5 GW new inflows in Q2; 70% DCR, 30% non-DCR; 5-5.5 GW deliverable in next 12-15 months
items.quote: Coming to our order book, as of 30th September 2026, our order book stood at approximately 10.4 gigawatts, supported by new order inflows of approximately 1.5 gigawatts during the quarter.

items.statement: Domestic module demand running at pace for ~64% YoY growth in CY2027; H1 CY2027 saw highest-ever 6-month solar installation at 27 GW AC (35 GW DC)
items.quote: Based on the current installation trajectory, domestic module demand is running a pace that could translate into approximately 64% year-on-year growth for this year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin maintained at ~35% in H1 FY27 and 35.3% in Q2 FY27; management confident margins will continue based on order book and cost efficiencies
items.quote: We have maintained EBITDA margins of approximately 35%, demonstrating the strength and consistency of our operating performance.

items.statement: Silver consumption reduced from 220mg to 60-65mg per cell; transition from M10R to G12R increasing cell wattage from 8W to 9.5W; 100% renewable power via open access reducing energy costs
items.quote: Today, w e are using around 60 milligrams to 65 milligrams. The second advantages is going to be there is what we are having M10R to be G12R. G12R where already we are reaching about 9.5 watt as in 8 watt what we used to have

items.statement: Module sales split: 75% institutional (utility/IPP and C&I), 25% retail (including KUSUM and Surya Ghar); >50% of capacity converted to G12R, rest M10R
items.quote: About 25% of our sales is to the markets of retail and KUSUM, and the remaining 75 split is for the institutional customers, such as both in the C&I and utility space.

items.statement: Creditor days reduced from 64 days in FY26 to 25 days in H1 FY27 through vendor negotiations for better pricing; finished goods inventory INR 860 crores out of total INR 1,884 crores
items.quote: Basically, it is all depends on how we negotiate with our vendors also. Sometimes we get some better price and then we reduce our credit days with them.

items.statement: ALMM-II implementation after December 2026 looks extremely unlikely; government emphasizing ALMM-III for ingots/wafers; DCR orders must be fulfilled regardless of ALMM extensions
items.quote: ALMM-II implementation after 2026 deferment looks extremely unlikely, especially that there is significant amount of time that is given for the industry to realign.

items.statement: Backward integration into ingot/wafer planned: 9 GW facility in two phases (5 GW + 4 GW) aligned with future cell requirements; timing guided by ALMM-III, market conditions, economic viability
items.quote: Our current plan envisages a 9 g igawatt of facility developed in two phases of 5 g igawatt and 4 gigawatt, aligned with our future cell manufacturing requirements.

items.statement: Operating cash flow increased 239% YoY to INR 410 crores in H1 FY27 from INR 121 crores in H1 FY26
items.quote: Net cash generated from the operating activities increased to approximately INR 410 crores in H1 of FY27, compared to INR 121 crores in H1 of FY 2026. This represents an improvement of approximately 239% year-on-year.

items.statement: Largest customer revenue share 44% in Q2 vs 19% in FY26; management says quarterly variation normal due to delivery timelines; payments secured via substantial down payments or LCs
items.quote: So, quarter-on-quarter, the revenue share keeps changing, of course, because the delivery timelines these thing, that will always be there. This is a ordinary course of business

items.statement: India needs 80-100 GW cell capacity for current demand trajectory; existing 41 GW includes ~16 GW Mono PERC to be phased out; potential shortage due to rising AC-DC ratios
items.quote: Well, actually, for our Indian demand to achieve the present numbers of the growth of present first half of the year or the forecasted one, we need our approximately 80 gigawatt to 100 gigawatt of capacity bare minimum

items.statement: State government capital subsidy of 25% received for earlier project; similar subsidies expected for upcoming projects but not modeled in guidance
items.quote: We have also declared that we have received capital subsidy for our earlier project from the State Government to the tune of 25%, and the s ame, similar subsidies are there, expected in the upcoming projects as well.

items.statement: Automated guided vehicles added in cell manufacturing reducing labor requirements; operational efficiencies implemented across departments
items.quote: And in our cell manufacturing, we have added automated guided vehicles, which reduce the people that are required to run the lines.

items.statement: Module utilization kept at 45-60% range to maintain flexibility for product configurations and opportunistic market approach; not targeting maximum utilization
items.quote: So, with that, keeping in mind, our utilizations will be broadly in the range of 45% to 60%.

items.statement: Forex gain contributed to lower other expenses in Q2; 100% renewable energy via open access for power consumption
items.quote: this time we have some forex gain also, which was relatively low last time, which is clubbed under the expense. That also making a difference for other expenses coming low.

items.statement: IPO proceeds deployed towards debt repayment strengthening balance sheet; finance cost reduced significantly YoY
items.quote: This reflects the strengthening of our balance sheet following the deployment of IPO proceeds towards debt repayment.

items.statement: Signed nearly INR1,000 crores deal with Sovereign AI company for Blackwell cluster through June 2029
items.quote: So we signed a nearly INR1,000 crores deal with a Sovereign AI company for the Blackwell cluster, which lasts through June 2029.

items.statement: Added Chief Revenue Officer, Field CTO, Founder's Office team and Strategic Advisor Anandamoy Roychowdhary
items.quote: We have a new Chief Revenue Officer. We have also added a team to the Founder's Office. We also have a Field CTO to help our customers understand our solutions better.

items.statement: Next lot of B200 GPUs expected to go live this quarter; 1,024 B200 planned GPUs deployment expected this quarter
items.quote: The next lot of B200 which we have already announced is expected to go live this quarter, hopefully soon.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 76.6%, up 141 bps QoQ; medium-term target 70%+ EBITDA margin
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR1,715 million, up 45% quarter-on-quarter with margin expanding to 76.6%. EBITDA margin expanded by 141 basis points compared to Q1 FY27.

items.statement: No forward guidance given on capex, MRR, or contracted revenue targets
items.quote: We do not give speculative capex guidance. We prefer to inform everyone when we have sufficiently fructified and solidified our deployment plan.

items.statement: International revenue roughly 20-25% of quarterly revenue
items.quote: So, in terms of international revenue, roughly around 20% to 25% of the revenue for the quarter is coming from international customers.

items.statement: India AI Mission revenue roughly 13-15% of quarterly revenue; continuing engagement with India AI customers
items.quote: So for the quarter, the revenue from India AI customers is roughly around 13% to 15%.

items.statement: Majority of GPUs run on TIR and Jarvis platforms; very little bare metal sold
items.quote: Majority of our GPUs today run on top of our platforms. There is very, very little bare metal that we sell today.

items.statement: Flagship Blackwell capacity fully utilized under INR1,000 crores contract; next B200 batch not yet contracted
items.quote: The flagship Blackwell capacity is fully utilized in the particular contract that was mentioned.

items.statement: Honouring customer commitments on pricing; uncontracted/short-term capacity expected to see earnings growth
items.quote: We want to obviously have a very good relationship with all our customers, which also means that we honour our commitment to our customers, whether contracted or verbal.

items.statement: Views global AI infrastructure TAM near $1 trillion; sees blue ocean with room for many players; not focused on peer comparison
items.quote: We are looking at a very large TAM, global market, where everyone who is a player in this market needs to find their own niche.

items.statement: Open to equity raise and off-balance-sheet funding; no mental limit on debt if cash flows support repayment
items.quote: We are super happy to explore any and everything with regard to what we are doing on tech, what we are doing in terms of funding for the GPUs.

items.statement: GPU order-to-deployment cycle typically 3-6 months; advance payment depends on vendor requirements
items.quote: We find that this order-to-deployment cycle can vary between 3 to 6 months, typically. And whether an advance needs to be paid depends on the vendor.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue INR2,238 million, up 411% YoY and 43% QoQ; H1 FY27 revenue INR3,805 million, up 376% YoY
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter stands at INR2,238 million, which is up by 411% year-on-year and 43% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: No fundamental supply chain challenges seen as insurmountable for near/medium term
items.quote: I don't see any fundamental supply chain challenges that are insurmountable for us in the near or medium term.

items.statement: Confirmed order book of USD1.135 billion (~INR10,700 cr) plus LOIs of USD575 million (export USD425m, domestic USD150m); with new USD50m LOI total potential ~INR17,000 cr
items.quote: The company has order book of confirmed order book of USD1.135 billion, which approximately INR 10,700 crores. And it further includes letter of intent for approximately USD575 million, which is mix of export and domestic business.

items.statement: LOIs of USD625m (USD480m export: USD430m CIS, USD50m SE Asia; USD145m domestic) expected to convert in weeks; production from Feb-Mar
items.quote: Out of this, 430 plus 50, let us say, USD480 million is export. And the USD 430 million is in CIS countries and this USD 50 million is from South East Asia.

items.statement: Domestic water infra demand soft; Jal Jeevan Mission fund releases gradual, orders now routed through states; ductile facilities fully booked for ~1 year but execution lagging due to EPC cash flow issues
items.quote: Second thing is that for some time, the orders would not be issued under Jal Jeevan Mission scheme. It would be from the State government side. So, state will raise the funds, they are issuing the orders, they will issue the orders.

items.statement: Export inquiry levels high in oil & gas and water sectors; LOIs received from CIS and South East Asia; Saudi anti-dumping duty on Indian DI pipes benefits Abu Dhabi facility
items.quote: Current inquiry levels are quite high and we are participating in all large inquiries. And we are hoping might be things may crystallize, but as of now, inquiry levels are high everywhere: oil and gas and water sector, especially in the export market.

items.statement: EBITDA margin compressed to 6.8% in Q2 (consol 8%); expects H2 better than H1, targeting double-digit margins from Q3/Q4 as oil & gas export mix improves
items.quote: We can expect Q3, Q4 onward that the margins will be moved towards, you know, double-digit and we are expecting and we expect that very soon this situation will be same what we were doing few quarters back.

items.statement: Gross profit per kg fell from INR51 to INR41 due to adverse mix (water heavy, domestic oversupply) and geopolitical disruption; expects improvement as oil & gas export orders execute
items.quote: Because of geopolitical situation and other domestic market situation, profit margin per kg has reduced drastically, which is reflected in the numbers also.

items.statement: Effective utilization ~67% (2.3mt capacity); best historical ~75% (1.8mt); expects execution improvement from Q4, but 80% utilization will take time
items.quote: So, 80% utilization and all, all depends on the execution of multiple orders. So, in the best-case scenario also, our execution level was somewhere 75%, not crossing that.

items.statement: Abu Dhabi seamless pipe plant: 300ktpa, ~USD330m investment, land secured, long-lead equipment procurement underway, financial closure in coming months, commercial ops FY28-29
items.quote: The project, with a proposed capacity of 300,000 tons per annum and an estimated investment of approximately USD330 million, is intended to strengthen the company's presence in Middle East oil and gas market.

items.statement: Saudi JV (51% Jindal Saw, 49% Buhur): two 300ktpa SAW pipe plants (helical & longitudinal), land secured, LCs established, interim financial closure in months, commercial ops targeting 2028-29
items.quote: The joint venture envisages setting up two advanced pipe manufacturing facilities, helical pipes and longitudinal pipes with a capacity of 300,000 metric ton each, catering to the region's growing water infrastructure and energy requirement.

items.statement: Saudi DI pipe finishing project put on hold; will serve Saudi market from Abu Dhabi facility instead
items.quote: Right now, considering the Saudi scenario, we have put on hold that venture. It in any case was very small. And till that time we finalize, let us say, our thoughts again, so we would be serving that market from the Abu Dhabi only.

items.statement: Surging coking coal costs squeezed DI pipe margins; pellet margins pressured by higher diesel prices, low Fe ore grade, high stripping ratio
items.quote: Surging raw material costs, particularly for coking coal have squeezed margins in the DI pipe business.

items.statement: Pellet business: high stripping ratio and low-grade iron ore lowering yield and raising operating cost; EC application filed with MoEF, ROM quantity unchanged
items.quote: We have high stripping ratio and low grade of iron ore. So, because of that, our margins are under pressure now. And the depth of the mine has gone up and we are working how to enhance or maintain the margins there.

items.statement: Reduction in current assets (inventory & receivables) in Q2; expects further reduction improving liquidity and reducing bank borrowings
items.quote: We have seen reduction of current assets in Q2, and we exp ect further reduction in the inventory and receivable amounts. This helps us to improve our liquidity position and thereby reduce bank borrowings

items.statement: Standalone net debt INR2,245 cr (Sep 26) vs INR2,346 cr (Jun 26); consol net institutional debt INR2,174 cr vs INR2,473 cr; CARE A1+/AA stable affirmed Jun 26
items.quote: As of 30th September '26, the company's standalone net debt narrowed to INR2,245 crores versus INR2,346 crores on 30th June '26.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia imposed anti-dumping duty 16-30% on Indian DI pipe exporters; Jindal Saw not affected as it supplies Saudi via Abu Dhabi subsidiary
items.quote: Anti-dumping duty has been imposed by Saudi Arabia government on the Indian exporters. But good thing is that since we did not export pipes from India to Saudi, so we are not into that anti-dumping duty imposition.

items.statement: MENA geopolitical escalation delaying 6 lakh ton job-work order to Saudi (buyer is Saudi JV partner); seeking alternative logistics routes; Abu Dhabi DI ops at ~50% utilization, sales restricted to trucking range
items.quote: Ongoing geopolitical tension in West Asia have worsened due to recent escalation s in Saudi Arabia, a region where we hold significant export order exposure. The main challenge is not other order cancellation, but rather delay in shipping and revenue recognition

items.statement: Abu Dhabi DI subsidiary order book USD195m (177kt) giving 9-12 months visibility; Q2 production 29kt vs 34kt in Q1
items.quote: As of September 2026, the subsidiary holds order book valued approximately USD195 million for corresponding 177,000 ton pipes, ensuring operational visibility for next 9 to 12 months.

items.statement: Jindal Hunting JV (51%): Q2 revenue INR9.7 cr, loss INR1.5 cr due to API license suspension; license reinstated Jun 26, expects improvement
items.quote: Jindal Hunting, a joint venture with Hunting Energy Services Private Limited, Singapore, in which Jindal Saw holds controlling interest of 51%, i t generated revenue of INR9.70 crores and a loss of INR1.5 crores in Q2 of FY27

items.statement: H1 sales mix skewed to low-margin domestic water; H2 expects improved oil & gas export volumes to shift mix and lift margins
items.quote: In H2, we are expecting a little bit change in terms of sales mix because this quarter sales mix was all together towards water sector, which is in general a low margin.

items.statement: Expects H2 FY27 better than H1; volumes in FY27 higher than FY26; margins to improve toward double-digits from Q3/Q4 as export oil & gas orders execute
items.quote: All these measures should start showing better results or demonstrate better volumes and thereby better margins. And we expect, as we have said last time also, we expect H2 to be better than H1.

items.statement: Saudi job-work buyer is also JV partner in Saudi pipe project; working on out-of-box logistics solution to resume shipments
items.quote: Incidentally, that the buyer is our joint venture partner in Saudi project also. We are we are, like, we are not replacing the capacity. For some time, the capacity might not be fully utilized.

items.statement: Export volumes 41% of order book but only 28% of value due to 6 lakh ton job-work order (conversion only, no raw material value); export orders generally CIF with freight cushion priced in
items.quote: Volumes are including the job-work order of roughly I6 lakh ton, where the volumes are high, however, this order is job-work order where only the job-work value is included. That's why in terms of value, it is 28%.

items.statement: Export orders priced CIF with sufficient cushion for volatile freight; domestic water oversupply pressuring prices; oil & gas export margins similar to domestic
items.quote: generally the trend in the export market is completely it is not FOB, it is generally a CIF, where the freight is also included. But since the current situation is more volatile, so we have taken a sufficient cushion about the pricing of all elemen ts which is on our part

items.statement: Abu Dhabi facility reduced operations to essential demand only, employee safety top priority; sales restricted to trucking-range countries
items.quote: Due to these circumstances, and with employee safety as our top priority, operations have been reduced to meet essential demand. The sales from Abu Dhabi plant are restricted to customers in the countrie s which are working -- which are within the trucking range

items.statement: Delhi High Court split verdict in Jindal ITF vs NTPC; matter referred to third judge, next hearing Jan 2027
items.quote: In this legal conflict, a division bench of Delhi High Court delivered a split verdict. Consequently, Chief Justice has referred the matter to a third judge, who has now been appointed. The next hearing is scheduled for January 2027.

items.statement: US subsidiaries (job-work: double jointing, coating, helical anchor) performing consistently, contributing positive EBITDA; Abu Dhabi facility EBITDA positive but margins reduced due to underutilization
items.quote: The US facilities which are under Jindal Saw fold, they are performing well. They are contributing positive. They are largely in job-work areas where double jointing, coating, and some helical anchor activities we are doing in various entities in US.

items.statement: Mid-double-digit consolidated revenue growth (~15%) expected for H2 FY27 with minimum EBITDA margin at FY26 level
items.quote: we are looking for mid -double-digit revenue growth, and this can be somewhere around 15% in that range

items.statement: MHE division EBIT margin guidance maintained at 22-24% for full year
items.quote: we have given guidance that we will maintain our margin throughout the year that is in the range of 22% to 24%

items.statement: Gear division open order book at INR1,056 crores as of Sep 30, 2026, up 37% YoY
items.quote: The open order book was INR1,056 crores as of September 30, 2026. This is up by 37% year-on-year

items.statement: MHE division open order book at INR579 crores as of Sep 30, 2026, up 27.3% YoY
items.quote: The open order book reached to INR 579 crores as of September 30, up 27.3% year -on-year

items.statement: Overseas order book at INR326 crores as of Sep 30, 2026
items.quote: Yes. So it is INR326 crores.

items.statement: Overseas order inflow grew 35% YoY in Q2 FY27, driven by Middle East and Americas
items.quote: Our overseas orders have seen an upsurge, okay, especially coming in from the Middle East and the Americas. Management: 35%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 140 bps YoY to 23.1% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA increased 17.7% to INR148 crores, while EBITDA margin expanded by 140 basis points to 23.1%.
