items.statement: Opex as percentage of average total assets increased to 4.9% in Q2 FY27 from 4.8% in Q1 FY27 due to branch expansion
items.quote: Opex as a percentage of average total assets in the ROA tree stood at 4.9% in quarter 2 compared to 4.8% in quarter 1, reflecting the full quarter impact of the branch and headcount additions.

items.statement: Total AUM grew 37% YoY to INR22,035 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our total disbursements grew 28% Y-o-Y to INR6,676 crores, and our AUM grew 37% Y-o-Y to INR22,035 crores.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM grew 77% YoY to INR11,917 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: And the gold AUM grew 77% Y-o-Y to INR11,917 crores.

items.statement: Mortgage AUM grew 13.5% YoY to INR9,982 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: And the AUM grew 13.5% Y-o-Y to INR9,982 crores.

items.statement: Doorstep gold loan AUM grew to INR1,851 crores
items.quote: Our doorstep gold loan offering maintained its momentum with AUM growing to INR1,851 crores.

items.statement: Opened 74 gold loan branches in Q2 FY27, total branch count now 831
items.quote: We have opened 74 branches this quarter, taking our total gold branch count to 831.

items.statement: Plan to add at least 150 more branches in H2 FY27
items.quote: In addition to the 74 branches we added in quarter 2, we propose to add at least another 150 branches in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM per branch increased to INR16.9 crores after branch openings
items.quote: Our AUM per branch after the branch opening stood at INR16.9 crores.

items.statement: Credit cost declined to INR27.1 crores (0.6% of average total assets annualized) in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our credit costs declined to INR27.1 crore in quarter 2, down 20.5% quarter-on-quarter from INR34.1 crore in quarter 1 due to improving collection efficiencies on the mortgage book.

items.statement: GNPA at 1.8% in Q2 FY27, up from 1.6% in Q1 FY27 due to gold loan transition
items.quote: On the asset quality, our GNPA stood at 1.8%, moving from 1.6% in Q1. The movement is primarily attributable to the ongoing transition in gold loan lending practices.

items.statement: NNPA at 1.2% with provision coverage ratio at 35.4% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: NNPA stands at 1.2%, with a provision coverage ratio at 35.4%.

items.statement: Gold loan Stage II increased from 2.7% to 3.6% and Stage III from 1.6% to 1.8% due to periodic interest model transition
items.quote: The increase in Stage II from 2.7% to 3.6% and in Stage III from 1.6% to 1.8% are entirely on account of this changed construct in gold loans.

items.statement: Gold loan LTV maintained at 68%, well within regulatory limits
items.quote: We continue to maintain a prudent risk profile with 68% LTV, well within the regulatory limits.

items.statement: Income generation loan (IGL) product structured at 75-85% LTV based on cash flow assessment
items.quote: When I say 85%, the loans are structured at 75%, 78%, 80% and 85%. That's how the product structure is, yes, and purely based on cash flows.

items.statement: Small ticket LAP minimum ticket size increased to INR8 lakhs from INR5 lakhs earlier
items.quote: We moved it up towards the 7 lakh s and 8 lakhs. You remember that we guided you that has played out in the average ticket size slightly moving up because now we are not doing anything below 8 lakhs

items.statement: Entered Eastern India in Q2 FY27, expanding geographical footprint
items.quote: This quarter also marks our entry into Eastern India, expanding our geographical footprint into newer and promising markets.

items.statement: Competitive intensity in gold loans heightened in Q2 FY27 across geographies and players
items.quote: In Q1, the intensity was there, but Q2, the intensity was a heightened one. All the kinds of yield growth strategies, lending practices, everything was played out across geographies.

items.statement: Small ticket LAP competitive intensity increased due to aggressive appetite from existing players and small finance banks
items.quote: The same players are operating in a similar market. That is why the intensity has increased. There is definitely a pressure on the yield.

items.statement: Fixed rate borrowings at 33%, MCLR-linked at 24%, remainder EBLR-linked
items.quote: Our fixed rate borrowings are 33% of our total borrowings. Of the balance, 67%, 24% is MCLR linked. So, the residual is only EBLR linked.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio improved to 4.6% from 4.9% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: This aided by higher co-lending in the gold portfolio, helped in bringing down the debt-equity ratio from 4.9% to 4.6%.

items.statement: Capital adequacy improved to 21% from 20.7% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: And improved capital adequacy to 21%, up from 20.7% in quarter 1.

items.statement: ROA expanded 24 bps QoQ to 2.8% in Q2 FY27, up from 2.1% nine quarters ago
items.quote: The ROA expanded sequentially quarter-on-quarter by 24 bps to 2.8%. The last 9 quarters have seen ROA slowly but steadily inching up from 2.1% to 2.8%.

items.statement: ROE expanded 153 bps QoQ to 17% in Q2 FY27, up from 10.9% nine quarters ago
items.quote: The ROE expansion sequentially has been 153 bps quarter-on-quarter to 17% in Q2. This also represents a steady increase from 10.9% ROE to 17% ROE over the last 9 quarters.

items.statement: Gold tonnage grew 16% YoY in Q2 FY27
items.quote: And the gold tonnage grew 16% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Profit after tax grew 63% YoY to INR130.8 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The quarter concluded with a profit after tax of INR130.8 crores, a Y-o-Y growth of 63%.

items.statement: Gold loan Stage II/III increases are technical delinquencies from customer behaviour transition, not structural credit concern
items.quote: Our gold GNPA at 0.5% reflects this transition, not a structural credit concern.

items.statement: No auction loss on principal or interest in last 6 years, management confident of maintaining record
items.quote: We have never had an auction loss on either principal or interest in the last 6 years. There is no intention to break that record.

items.statement: Expect Q3 and Q4 volumes stronger than Q2; H2 historically 20% up on H1
items.quote: Based on our current indication, we expect Q3 and Q4 volumes to be stronger than Q2. Overall volumes and historically also H2 is always 20% up on H1.

items.statement: Expect trailer segment revenue to stay at Q2 levels (INR115-116 cr) for rest of FY27
items.quote: For this financial year, we see that -- at least for this financial year, we see the numbers to stay like this. Unless -- unforeseen can happen.

items.statement: Expect receivable days around 80 and working capital cycle less than 90-95 days
items.quote: So with now things improving as far as the trailer segment, it would be getting better. And there is a small portion of our export business, which we still have receivable days above 120. So that would remain -- but that portion is only 4%, 4.5% of our business right now. But overall, we see that our receivable days will be at around 80 and our working capital cycle should be lesser than 90, 95 da

items.statement: Expect exports to grow 45% YoY this year
items.quote: Year-on-year, we expect this year to be 45% higher than our previous year.

items.statement: Seamless tube production trials planned for February or March 2027
items.quote: The sizing mill and straightening mills have been received and installed, and we plan to undertake production trials in February or March of 2027.

items.statement: Plan to switch to 100% extruded beam process for trailer axles by Q3 or Q4
items.quote: This particular aspect of business by Q3 or Q4, we will be producing our trailer axles in this methodology only by the extruded beam process.

items.statement: Expect utilization levels to improve progressively over coming 2 quarters
items.quote: For the half year, the investments in our capacity expansions and backward integration initiatives have started contributing to our operational readiness, and we expect our utilization levels to improve progressively over the coming 2 quarters.

items.statement: Spent INR120 crores on seamless tube facility out of INR170 crore budget as of Q2
items.quote: Our own contribution is about INR60 crores, okay, INR60 crores plus INR50 crores -- INR70 crores, we have taken as our -- from the term loan, INR70 crores plus INR50 crores, INR120 crores out of the INR170 crores.

items.statement: Plan INR110 crores capex in H2 FY27 including INR50-60 crores via warrants/pref shares and INR50 crores balance on seamless tube
items.quote: Close to INR60 crores we are planning on an immediate capex via warrants and pref shares, which we would be spending between the next 2 quarters. This is basically to cater to the increased demand which we are foreseeing in the industry as well as in the trailer segment. And also on -- as we just mentioned on our seamless project, we are looking at a further balanced capex of close to INR50-odd cr

items.statement: Cold drawn tube forward integration to cost INR20-25 crores
items.quote: We will be spending close to, I think, it's about INR24 crores, INR25, INR20-odd crores in this area, in this cold drawn tube and the metal treatment involved with it.

items.statement: Extruded axle beam capacity utilization at 65-80% of current 4,400 axles/month output
items.quote: We are making currently 4,000 trailer axles, 4,400 trailer axles per month. On that, we are utilizing between 65% to 80% of our extruded beams, which we basically are mentioning that in the next 1 or 2 quarters, we will be switching to 100%.

items.statement: Tipping jack capacity set at 800 units; expect 50-60% utilization by Q4
items.quote: We've set a capacity of close to 800 numbers. We should be at at least 50%, 60% of that capacity by quarter 4.

items.statement: Seamless tube Phase 1 capacity at 30% of 1 lakh total capacity
items.quote: Phase 1 would be 50% of that capacity? Kunal Rai: No, no. 30% of it, 30%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 13% in Q2 FY27; difficult to guide return to 14-15% due to steel and conversion cost escalations
items.quote: EBITDA for this quarter was at INR30.6 crores with a margin of 13%.

items.statement: Backward integration via seamless tubes expected to add 3-4% margin on axle business
items.quote: On the overall business, we should be having a margin of approximately 3% to 4% once we use our own seamless tubes for it.

items.statement: Seamless tube captive production expected to be 8-10% cheaper than current buying prices
items.quote: The benefit of it in terms of -- as compared to the existing price that we buy it, it should be at around approximately 8% to 10% lesser than -- or you could say more competitive than existing buying prices.

items.statement: Price revisions with OEMs and Tier 1s concluded; expected to support Q3 and Q4 margins
items.quote: While we have witnessed some pressures from rising consumable and commodity costs, the price revisions, including -- concluded with the OEMs and Tier 1 customers are expected to support us during the Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Steel prices increasing every quarter; only partial compensation received in Q1 and Q2
items.quote: Steel has been increasing, you could say, every quarter. There has been only a part of the compensation on steel as a commodity, which we have received in quarter 1. There will be further -- in quarter 1 and quarter 2, both, there's just a part of it.

items.statement: Conversion cost settlements with OEMs and Tier 1s recently concluded; impact expected in Q3 and Q4
items.quote: We have very recently settled with most of our OEMs and Tier 1 companies on a conversion front as well. That impact would be coming in our upcoming quarters, that is quarter 3, mostly in quarter 3 and quarter 4.

items.statement: Trailer segment Q2 volumes exceeded earlier record levels of Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our Q2 volumes have exceeded the earlier record levels of Q4 of '26.

items.statement: Receivable days improved from 110+ in H1 FY26 to ~81 days in Q2 FY27; H1 at ~90 days
items.quote: If you look into our receivable days, which was in H1 of last year, they were in excess of 110 days. And if you look into -- for the quarter, it's almost come down back to around 81 days. And overall for H1 period, it's at around 90 days.

items.statement: Total debt ~INR115 crores as of Sep 30 (INR80 cr term loan + INR32 cr working capital); expect ~INR165-170 crores by FY27 end
items.quote: If you look into our balance sheet, our total term loan is at INR80 crores. And then we have our working capital and CC limit, which is at approximately INR32 crores. The further which will go on is basically on the balance on the seamless tube.

items.statement: Largest customer ~15-16% of top line; tractor segment ~10-11% of revenue all OEMs; CV business with both OEMs and Tier 1s
items.quote: And our largest customer is approximately 15%, 16% of our top line.

items.statement: Trailer axle competitors: York (market leader), Tata Motors, BPW, Hendrickson; component business has diversified competitors by product family
items.quote: On the trailer side, obviously, there is York who are the market leaders in this segment, and there's Tata Motors as well who are in this business. There's BPW and Hendrickson also who are in the supply of axles and suspensions. On our component business, because of our diversified product range, we have different competitors for different products of ours where with a lot of products, we do enjoy

items.statement: Q2 revenue mix: trailer segment 49%, component business 51%; tractor ~10-11% of total
items.quote: If you look into our sales segment mix for this specific quarter, our trailer segment has contributed close to 49% of our revenue, while the component business contributed the balance 51%.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue INR419.4 crores, EBITDA INR53.32 crores, PAT INR33.16 crores
items.quote: If we look into the H1 highlights, the revenue total stands at INR419.4 crores as compared to INR270 crores of last year. EBITDA stands at INR53.32 crores and PAT stands at INR33.16 crores.

items.statement: Maintains mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth guidance for H2 FY27 despite strong H1 overachievement
items.quote: we definitely stay true on the guidance, that yes, H1 has been far stronger than the guidance and we expect the trends to continue but definitely mid-to-high teens (EBITDA) for the balance of the year is something that we are anchored towards.

items.statement: Q3 FY27 trending ahead of pace with double-digit RevPAR growth expected, driven by events and festive demand
items.quote: we are very much on track for double-digit growth in terms of RevPAR in Q3 as well.

items.statement: H1 FY27 operating EBITDA margin expanded 246 bps; Q2 margin at 46%, up 118 bps YoY
items.quote: For the first half as a whole, operating revenue grew 30% and operating EBITDA grew 38%, with margin expanding by 246 basis points.

items.statement: Over 1,000 keys under development across marquee destinations including Srinagar, Bandhavgarh, Sikkim, Ayodhya, Agra, Ranthambore, Tadoba, BKC Mumbai
items.quote: we now have more than 1,000 keys under development across marquee destinations.

items.statement: Contracted pipeline capex of INR 1,432 crores for five owned hotels; INR 150 crores spent, INR 450 crores by end FY27, INR 600 crores in FY28
items.quote: the capex for our five contracted pipelines, is Agra, Srinagar, Ayodhya, Ranthambore, Bandhavgarh is around INR1,432 crores. We have spent around INR150 crores. By the end of this year, we will be spending around INR450 crores. Next year, we are looking at spending around INR600 crores.

items.statement: Corporate rate negotiations for CY27 targeting mid-to-high double-digit growth; shifted 60-70% of static corporate rates to dynamic pricing
items.quote: we are pitching for mid-to-high double-digit growth rates in terms of our ask rates, but the negotiations are on.

items.statement: Direct booking contribution via brand website rose to 15.1% of room revenue in H1 FY27 from 10.5% YoY, reducing third-party channel dependency
items.quote: For H1 FY27, the contribution to The Leela brand website to room revenue rose to 15.1% from 10.5% last year, and from 5.5% 2 years ago.

items.statement: BKC Mumbai JV to seek shareholder approval for FSI purchase; Leela and Brookfield 50-50 owners; Leela to contribute share of FSI cost
items.quote: we will now look to buy the entire FSI required for the project. Since this is a material transaction with a related party, with the JV entity, Leela will shortly reach out to the shareholders for an approval of investment.

items.statement: Evaluating acquisition and brownfield opportunities to bolt on to existing 5,200+ key pipeline targeting FY30 EBITDA aspiration of INR 2,000 crores
items.quote: we are evaluating several opportunities both on the asset-right side as well as possibly acquisitions, or brownfield acquisitions, which will be bolting-on to all what we already have.

items.statement: Leela Centre of Excellence delivered 4,800+ man-hours training to 280+ participants; ranked Top 100 India's Best Workplaces for Women 2026
items.quote: The Leela Centre of Excellence has already delivered over 4,800 man-hours of training and engaged more than 280 participants since launch. We were also recognized amongst the Top 100 of India's Best Workplaces for Women 2026.

items.statement: International business showing low double-digit growth excluding BRICS; targeting return to 50-50 domestic-international mix over time
items.quote: International business has also started slowly trickling in. In the last quarter, there was a low double-digit growth in terms of international business (even excluding BRICS). We eventually believe that we would again go back to our 50-50 kind of a mix of international to India.

items.statement: Finance cost broadly stable at INR 384 million in Q2; H1 finance cost fell 37% to INR 777 million due to IPO debt reduction
items.quote: For the first half, finance costs fell 37% to INR 777 million, reflecting the debt reduction through the IPO.

items.statement: Dubai JV share of loss improved vs last quarter; hotel operating at high occupancy via local staycations but ADRs lagging on low international tourism
items.quote: Our share of loss from joint ventures is primarily attributable to our 25% stake in the Dubai Palm Jumeirah hotel and has improved versus the last quarter. The asset is operating at high occupancy through local staycations, though ADRs are lagging given lower international tourism demand.

items.statement: Arq By The Leela New Delhi operational; Arq Chennai opening Q3 FY27; Aujasya wellness Bengaluru and renewable energy Chennai/Coorg advancing
items.quote: Arq By The Leela in New Delhi is operational, and the Arq Chennai is scheduled to open this quarter. Development is advancing well on the Aujasya wellness facility in Bengaluru, and on renewable energy initiatives in Chennai and Coorg.

items.statement: Raw material basket expected to increase 4-5% in Q3 FY27; NSR planned increase of 4-5% in Q3 FY27
items.quote: And our guidance going ahead for Q3 would be a further increase of about 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Capex guidance for balance of FY27 is around Rs 500 crore
items.quote: This is going to be roughly around INR500 crores for the balance period.

items.statement: Volume growth from capex expected at 1:1 to 1:1.1 asset turnover; Rs 1,130 crore expansion underway and Rs 5,000 crore planned in phases
items.quote: The volume growth on account of the capex would be roughly around 1:1 the asset turn, which we are expecting rather 1:1.1 you can consider because we are now taking up expansions immediately for INR1,130 crores, which is going on and then thereafter in phases for around INR5,000 crores capex.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 7.1% in Q2 FY27 from 6.8% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA margins (Consolidated) were recorded at 7.1% v/s 6.8% in Q1FY27.

items.statement: Management expects some improvement in EBITDA margins in Q3 FY27 despite raw material cost pressures
items.quote: So I see that some basic points going forward in Q3, definitely, there would be some improvement in terms of the margins.

items.statement: Raw material basket increased ~9% QoQ in Q2 FY27, cumulative ~30% in last 6 months; NSR increased 7% QoQ in Q2, cumulative 11-12% in 6 months
items.quote: We have seen the raw material whole basket increased by 9% on a Q-o-Q basis, which is on a Q1 to Q2 basis. We have seen, obviously, because of the inflationary pressure and supply chain constraint because of the West Asia. Cumulatively, we have seen a staggering 30% increase in the last 6 months.

items.statement: Crude-based raw materials constitute 65-70% of basket; carbon black, synthetic rubber, butyl, steel cord all increased YoY and QoQ
items.quote: As you know that crude oil-based raw material is almost in the tune of about 65% to 70%. And there, definitely carbon black, synthetic rubber, butyl, steel cord, they have all increased on a Y-o-Y basis and even on a Q-o-Q basis.

items.statement: Demand healthy and steady for Q3 FY27; Q4 expected to be strong due to OEM year-end closing
items.quote: We see the demand being steady in Q3. And Q4, as we know, that will be the year-end closing for most of the OEMs also, there will be good demand coming in.

items.statement: Replacement market seeing healthy growth momentum continuing; TBR high single-digit, PCR mid-single-digit medium-term outlook
items.quote: So replacement market, we are seeing a healthy growth momentum, which would continue. And Q2 has definitely shown that. We are seeing category-wise, we are seeing a high single digit coming in the TBR. We are seeing a mid-single digit in the passenger car coming in the medium-term outlook.

items.statement: Highest-ever consolidated revenue of Rs 4,850 crore in Q2 FY27, up 20% YoY; domestic sales up 32% YoY with OE up 65%
items.quote: We have achieved our highest-ever turnover of Rs.4,850 crore, up by 20% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: TBR OE volumes up 76% YoY, PCR OE volumes up 35% YoY; EV volumes surged 24% QoQ
items.quote: TBR and PCR segments continue to remain the cornerstone of our products strategy with an extremely robust double-digit OE volumes growth of 76% and 35%, respectively, on YoY basis.

items.statement: Domestic volumes up 22% YoY (OE 25%, replacement 20%); export volumes up 7% QoQ; 2/3W replacement volumes more than 2x YoY
items.quote: Domestic markets recorded a healthy volumes growth of 22%, driven by a robust 25% in OE Market and a similar 20% in replacement markets.

items.statement: Capacity utilization in India above 90% across key segments including TBR, PLR, 2/3W
items.quote: Capacity utilization levels in India remained high at above 90% across key segments including TBR, PLR, 2/3W etc.

items.statement: Rs 1,400 crore projects recently completed; Rs 1,130 crore expansion underway; Rs 5,000 crore planned in phases
items.quote: And the 2 nd point is because we have undertaken certain expansion projects for TBR and PCR in addition to what we have completed recently for INR1,400 crores projects.

items.statement: Net debt increased Rs 751 crore QoQ to Rs 5,696 crore due to 30% raw material price increase raising inventory value and higher volumes; operating leverage also a factor
items.quote: So, two points, one is that why the net debt has gone up, because of the 30% increase in the raw material prices and therefore, the value of the raw material inventory and the final product inventory has gone up.

items.statement: Inventory increased due to 30% raw material price rise in 6 months, volume growth, and strategic raw material inventory build
items.quote: Inventory has gone up for 2 reasons, one, there has been an increase in the raw material prices to the extent of about 30% in the last 6 months since the West Asia crisis started and also because of volume increase, and Second, we have also kept some strategic inventory in raw material.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt Rs 5,696 crore as of 30.09.2026, up Rs 751 crore QoQ; net debt to equity 0.94x; ROCE 12%, ROE 8.7%
items.quote: Consolidated Net debt as on 30.09.26 stood at Rs.5,696 Cr, up by Rs.751 crore on QoQ basis. The overall debt of the company has moved primarily on account of increased capex led long-term borrowings and additional working capital requirement for higher raw material prices and higher volumes.

items.statement: Exports from India up 14% QoQ; Mexico operations revenue Rs 479 crore, EBITDA Rs 23 crore; Mexican peso appreciated ~10% vs USD in 6 months
items.quote: Despite geopolitical uncertainties, export from India were up by 14% on a sequential basis over Q1FY27.

items.statement: JK Tornel Mexico-to-US exports showing triple-digit volume growth QoQ; expecting normal sales comparable to last year by Q4 FY27
items.quote: And just to add to it that –sales from Mexico to U.S., which we call it as an export from Mexico, there we've had a triple-digit growth in terms of volume push.

items.statement: Premium SKUs (16 inch+) constitute ~30% of passenger line volumes in H1 FY27, growing at ~20% CAGR over 2-3 years
items.quote: At JK Tyre, nearly 30% of passenger line volumes sold in H1 are towards premium SKUs i.e. 16 inch & above tyres. This segment has maintained a high CAGR of nearly 20% over the past 2-3 years.

items.statement: Standalone revenue mix: replacement 60%, OEM 30%, exports 10%; category mix: TBR 56%, PLR 28%, 2/3W 6%, non-truck bias 10%
items.quote: Market mix for the replacement market mix is 60%, the OEM is 30% and export is 10% of the total revenue on standalone basis.

items.statement: Added 250+ Pitstops, 80+ new dealers (50% rural), expanded OTR range with premium application-specific products; MG Hector Tomahawk launched on Ranger HPe EV tyre
items.quote: In order to strengthen our customer reach, we have further added numerous brand shops, 250+ Pitstops and several mobility fleet accounts during the quarter. Apart from the above, 80+ new dealers have been onboarded in Q2 out of which nearly 50% are rural dealers & distributors.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA Rs 343 crore, up 28% QoQ; PAT Rs 60 crore, up 40% QoQ; EPS Rs 2.29 vs Rs 1.55 QoQ; cash profits Rs 234 crore vs Rs 169 crore QoQ
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA for Q2FY27 was recorded at Rs.343 crore as compared to Rs.268 crore in Q1FY27, up by 28% sequentially.

items.statement: West Asia conflict creating inflationary pressures via commodity prices and supply chain disruptions; raw material costs up 30% in 6 months
items.quote: The steep increase in the prices of key raw materials due to West-Asia crisis and continued volatility have triggered the inflationary pressures, impacting the profitability margins in the near term.

items.statement: Evaluating India-UK FTA benefits; developing Europe-specific SKUs to leverage tariff elimination on Indian tyres entering UK
items.quote: Yes, we are evaluating India - U.K. trade tariff agreement right now. And as I had mentioned earlier in the call that we are developing and developed many Europe specific SKU's . So that we will be definitely taking advantage of the welcoming FTA.

items.statement: JK Tornel modernization/expansion project progressing as planned to improve revenue and profitability
items.quote: Parallelly, our upgradation cum modernisation expansion project at JK Tornel is progressing as planned, which will help in improving the revenue and profitability.

items.statement: Awarded Mahatma Award for Community Initiatives 2026 for fourth consecutive year
items.quote: It is with utmost pride we announce that JK Tyre has been awarded with the momentous 'Mahatma Award for Community Initiatives 2026' for the 4th time in a row.

items.statement: Targeting 11 million ton net steel production in FY27 with H2 run rate of 6 million tons
items.quote: Our aim is to reach to about 11-million-ton production in this financial year as targeted earlier. We have reached to a level of about 4.79 million tons in H1. And the next, that is H2, we are aiming for 6 million tons.

items.statement: Annual growth capex guidance of INR 7,500-10,000 crores funded through internal accruals
items.quote: Our stated framework envisages annual growth capex of approximately INR 7,500 crores to INR 10,000 crores, primarily funded through internal accruals, while seeking to maintain net debt to EBITDA below 1.5x through the cycle.

items.statement: New Angul blast furnace ramping to 12,000 tpd by December; 192 km slurry pipeline commissioned
items.quote: Hopefully, we will ramp it up in this particular month, say, today is 23rd, so I think in 7 days' time, we should reach to about 10,500 tons per day. And in November, we are aiming for 11,000 tons and then December 12,000 tons per day.

items.statement: Record quarterly sales of INR 19,448 crores; 2.38 million tons volume; targeting INR 1 lakh crore annual sales
items.quote: The company has done wonderfully well in last quarter. We have done a record sales in the history of this company in any quarter in the last so many years. That is INR 19,448 crores. So, I think we are now on a path to reach to INR 1 lakh crores per year of sales.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA INR 2,504 crores, up 34% YoY; EBITDA per ton INR 10,529, up 5% YoY
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA stood at INR 2,504 crores, up 34% Y-o-Y, while adjusted EBITDA per ton increased 5% Y-o-Y to INR 10,529 per ton.

items.statement: Coking coal cost impact $20-25/ton expected in Q3; diesel impact $4-5/ton from West Asia conflict
items.quote: said $12. This quarter, we are saying $20 per ton, which we expect an impact on account of the diesel. Amit Murarka: Sure. And this is beyond the coking coal inflation, right, just to be sure. Sandeep Modi: No, coking coal, I said $20 to $25. And for the West Asia conflict, which I think you are reflecting more on the diesel and other part, we did not give INR 1,200, INR 1,300. We said around $4 t

items.statement: Switched from propane (INR 100/kg) to coal syngas (INR 30/kg) saving INR 70/kg for downstream lines
items.quote: You see the propane prices have gone up to a level of about INR 100 per kilo. And equivalent when we make coal gas, that is called syngas, then equivalent, we were getting in INR 30 a kilo. So that advantage was INR 70 a kilo.

items.statement: Flat product mix target 65% (including plates) vs 35% long; value-added mix 57% in Q2
items.quote: We are now aiming to increase our overall product mix towards flat products. Though today also, we are at a level of about 60% -40%. Now we'll be reaching somewhere about 65%-35%, 65% flat products, including plates and 35% will be long products.

items.statement: Exporting ~100,000 tons/month (HRC, plates, rails, structures); hopeful on EU FTA and quota relaxation
items.quote: The exports are also picking up. We are doing about 100,000 tons of export every month, mainly hot-rolled coils , plates and some quantity in rails and the structures. We are hopeful the honourable Commerce Minister, Mr. Piyush Goyal, is already in And I think he is negotiating with EU on the basis of the mother of all deals, what we signed is FTA.

items.statement: Net debt reduced INR 1,141 crores to INR 14,786 crores; net debt/EBITDA improved to 1.51x
items.quote: Our consolidated net debt declined by INR 1,141 crores from INR 15,927 crores at the end of June to INR 14,786 crores as at September end. Net debt-to-EBITDA ratio improved from 1.71x to 1.51x.

items.statement: Government providing 50% royalty exemption for coal gasification; Roida iron ore mine needs forest clearance by January
items.quote: Yes, there's no problem. First of all, yes, you're right. Government is open to provide coal and with the exemption of 50% of royalty. So, this is one. And secondly, from our own mines also, we'll be in a position to feed the coal gasification. No problem.

items.statement: Manpower stable with no exodus; middle management being elevated to higher responsibilities
items.quote: The manpower is stable. There is no churning. The people from the middle management and upper middle management, those who are at a level about AGM, DGM, general managers, Assistant Vice President , they are being elevated to take the higher responsibilities. And there is very positive atmosphere in the organization.

items.statement: Water availability risk mitigated: using 31 MLD vs 59 MLD allocation; slurry pipeline returns water for recycling
items.quote: So, first of all, I'll tell you, we do not need 59 MLD now. We are using only 31 MLD, which is sufficient. And in next year, we'll be using at least 15% less. Why? Because we are pumping water from Barbil. So, this water will be surplus.

items.statement: Industry steel demand growing ~10% YoY; JSP production up 20% YoY outperforming industry
items.quote: I think it is now around 10% Y-o-Y basis, there's a growth. Though our production has gone up by 20%. The industry overall growth is about 10%. So, we are aiming that we'll continue making such performance in other 2 quarters also, that is Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Domestic demand strong; Q3/Q4 optimistic on construction pickup post-monsoon and festival season
items.quote: Historically, quarter 2 used to be very bad because of rainy season, constructions were at very low level. So, cement and steel, I mean, the rebars, they will always suffer in Q2. But now Q3 is very optimistic. It's a festival season, the building construction in the country going very well.

items.statement: TMT production cut from 220,000 to 120,000 tons/month; shifted to value-added flats and plates for projects
items.quote: So, I would say that now we are making only 120,000 tons per month of TMT. And earlier, we were making 220,000 tons. So, 100,000 tons TMT, whatever the steel was going to be utilized for TMT, that we are now utilizing in flat products, that is for plates as well as for hot-rolled coils.

items.statement: India well-positioned to supply Europe's 28 million ton steel deficit; CBAM remains issue but solutions expected
items.quote: There's a steel deficit of about 28 million tons in Europe. And I think India stands the first chance to supply the right and good quality of steel to Europe. CBAM is an issue today. But overnight, the CBAM cannot be diluted.

items.statement: New pellet plant (Barbil) targeting June 2027 commissioning; all current pellet output consumed internally
items.quote: And as far as the new pellet plant is concerned, yes, it is on the way. On the way means it has come up. Hopefully, by June next year, this will be fully commissioned. So, by March, we will be doing the complete installation. And maybe end of March or early April, we'll start our trials. And June, it should be in commercial production.

items.statement: Transmission capex expected at INR14,000 crore for FY27 with INR8,000-9,000 crore in H2
items.quote: We expect to do total capex of transmission in the range of about INR14,000 crore. So we will be doing about INR8,000 crores to INR9,000 crores of capex in second half.

items.statement: Smart Metering installation target 8-9 million meters in FY27 with balance 4-4.5 million in H1 FY28
items.quote: So we plan for about 80 to 90 lakh meters this year. And the balance about 40 lakh, 45 lakh, we hope that we will be able to complete in the next half year.

items.statement: Energy Solutions platform targets 7,000-8,000 MW consumer-side tie-ups over 3-4 years
items.quote: So we will continue to scale up this volume, and we will reach to about total aggregate capacity on both sides about 7,000 megawatts to 8,000 megawatts of tie up over 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex deployment at all-time high of INR7,850 crore across all businesses
items.quote: the capex in this first half of the year in the all-time high. We have deployed about INR7,850 crores of capex in among all our businesses.

items.statement: Transmission capex pipeline projects INR6,000 crore in H2 FY27 and INR18,000-19,000 crore in FY28
items.quote: we actually expect to incur to INR6,000 crores additional capex in the second half of this year and another INR18,000 crores to INR19,000 crores in the FY '28.

items.statement: Transmission order book at INR87,000 crore including recently won Vizag Pendurthi and Satara projects
items.quote: And with these two projects, our order book remains at about INR87,000 crores.

items.statement: Smart Metering delivered 14.8 million meters (60% of order book), balance to complete in 12-14 months
items.quote: Smart Metering, we have now delivered about 14.8 million meters so far. And around 60 percentage of our order book, that we have delivered and balance portion, we wish to complete in another 12 to 14-month time.

items.statement: Energy Solutions platform Q2 revenue >INR2,000 crore, EBITDA >INR800 crore
items.quote: During this quarter, the platform delivered revenue of over INR2,000 crores and EBITDA of over INR800 crores.

items.statement: Mumbai distribution consumption increased >10% in H1 FY27 while losses reduced to 4.29%
items.quote: Our Distribution losses in Mumbai has reduced further to 4.29 percentage in the first half. And this despite the fact that consumption has also increased by more than 10 percentage.

items.statement: Energy Solutions consumer stack: 2,500 MW MSEDCL PPA, 750 MW AEML PPA, 400 MW C&I clients, targeting data centers
items.quote: a diverse set of consumer stack even today. So one, obviously, you have 2,500 megawatts of the MSEDCL PPA, 750 megawatt of AEML, so that's 3,250 megawatts. We are targeting multiple data center customers. We are in advanced discussions with them. Then further, we also have close to 400 megawatts of C&I clients

items.statement: MSEDCL PPA phased: 1,000 MW from Feb-end, 1,000 MW from Apr-end, 500 MW from Jul-end next year
items.quote: 2.5 gigawatts MSEDCL signed, the capacity starts being deployed from end of February this year, 1,000 megawatts, then 1,000 megawatts from end of April and then another 500 megawatts end of July in the next year.

items.statement: Intrastate transmission projects offer better ROE than interstate due to state regulatory framework
items.quote: So on intrastate, typically it is a little better as compared to interstate because, obviously, those developers will see as an state regulatory versus central regulatory landscape. So typically in state, the ROE would trend a little better.

items.statement: S&P Global Electric Utility ESG rank #1 globally with 90/100 score vs industry average 40
items.quote: we are happy to say that now in S&P Global Electric Utility category, we are number one globally, getting 90 out of 100 rank, where industry average is about 40

items.statement: Transmission commissioning delays due to ROW issues in Gujarat (Halvad); resolution expected soon at government level
items.quote: Halvad is stacked up because of the ROW problem. And we expect resolution very soon. In fact, it is being discussed at Government of Gujarat as well as our Government of India level very frequently.

items.statement: Potential Smart Metering acquisition opportunities being explored beyond bidding
items.quote: And there could also be an opportunity of acquisition in the market on top of what we get here through bidding.

items.statement: MAT credit assets of ~INR1,500 crore recognized for MEGPTCL and ATIL under new tax regime with corresponding recoverable liability
items.quote: See, there are two companies, MEGPTCL and ATIL, where we have decided to go to the new tax regime and recognize the past paid MAT assets in the books of account which are close to around INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: NIM expected to recover to approximately 5.8% by Q4 FY27 as excess liquidity is deployed and repo rate increases materialize
items.quote: Just in terms of how do we see NIMs going forward, we see this recovering to approximately 5.8% by Q4 as some of these excess liquidity would have been definitely put to use by them and also the expected repo rate increase, which we also are factoring for the course of the year.

items.statement: Bank aims to operate at 55% incremental cost-to-income ratio for FY27
items.quote: So we feel overall this year, i.e., in '27, we can operate the bank at 55% cost -income ratio.

items.statement: Loan growth visibility of at least 20% and deposit growth capacity of 21-22% on core basis
items.quote: So 20 -20 both sides. So you know that the income will keep flowing in strongly.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of 1.5% to 1.6% maintained for FY27
items.quote: So we are very comfortable with our 1.5% to 1.6% credit cost guidance?

items.statement: NIM moderated to 5.58% in Q2 FY27 from 5.90% in Q1 FY27 due to FCNR impact, excess liquidity, asset mix change and day count
items.quote: The net interest margin for the quarter was 5.58% as compared to 5.90% in the previous quar ter, excluding the income tax refund, which we have reported

items.statement: FCNR lending caused 16 bps NIM drag, excess liquidity parking caused 7 bps drag, asset mix change 5 bps, day count 4 bps
items.quote: So to summarize, 16 bps is because of FCNR lending, 7 bps is because of excess liquidity, 4 bps is because of day count convention and 5 bps is because of other asset mix changes.

items.statement: FCNR impact on ROA estimated at only 2 bps as expanded balance sheet reduces opex and credit cost ratios
items.quote: And hence, we have estimated that the overall impact on the ROA could be very minimal as low as 2 basis points.

items.statement: FCNR deposits provide ~1% cost of funds benefit vs domestic deposits including statutory benefits
items.quote: Pursuant to the FCNR scheme, we also have estimated an additional benefit of 1%, including statutory benefits, which could accrue to us if we compare this with a normal deposit, which we would have raised otherwise.

items.statement: Loan book grew 30.1% YoY and 13.6% QoQ including FCNR; 22.2% YoY and 5.7% QoQ excluding FCNR
items.quote: Moving on to loans. That registered a strong growth of 30.1% on a Y-o-Y basis and 13.6% on a Q-on-Q basis, including FCNR, and that book has now reached about INR3.47 lakh crores.

items.statement: Mortgage, vehicle loans, consumer loans, business banking and wholesale loans each grew >30% YoY
items.quote: The incremental growth on the loan side during the quarter was primarily driven by mortgage, vehicle loans, consumer loans and a slightly faster growth in business banking and wholesale loans, which individually grew by more than 30% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Mobilized INR34,390 crores (USD3.6B) FCNR(B) deposits, constituting 10% of total deposits; extended USD2.6B (INR25,000 crores) leverage to NRI customers
items.quote: During the quarter, the bank mobilized INR34,390 crores, which is about USD3.6 billion of FCNR (B) deposit under this scheme. This constituted about 10% of the overall deposit that we have at September 30, 2026.

items.statement: Credit cards in force crossed 5 million; outstanding book at INR9,875 crores; spends grew 15% YoY
items.quote: happy to report that the cards in force crossed 5 million during the quarter. The book on an outstanding basis stood at INR9,875 crores, and the credit card spends grew at a healthy pace of about 15% on a Y -o-Y basis.

items.statement: GNPA improved 19 bps to 1.32% QoQ; Net NPA improved 4 bps to 0.40%; SMA-1&2 reduced to 0.58%
items.quote: On a headline basis, the gross NPA ratio of the bank improved by about 19 basis points from 1.51% reported in Q1 to 1.32% in Q2 and by 9 bps if we exclude FCNR leverage from the denominator.

items.statement: Collection efficiency stable at 99.5% for retail; MFI SMA-1&2 normalized to 0.6% from 0.7%; net slippage ratio stable at 1.6%
items.quote: The collection efficiency for the current bucket for retail continues to hold well. It has been now stable around the 99.5% for many quarters.

items.statement: Bank holds INR515 crores contingency provision; credit cost improved to 1.38% (1.30% excl. FCNR) on average funded assets
items.quote: The bank continues to hold the contingency provision of INR515 crores created last quarter. This is on a prudent basis, considering the evolving macroeconomic and the geopolitical uncertainties.

items.statement: No specific capex guidance; opex grew 16% YoY and 3.7% QoQ to INR5,942 crores; incremental cost-to-income at 55% for H1
items.quote: Moving on, the opex for the quarter was at INR5,942 crores. This grew by 16% on a Y-o-Y basis and by 3 .7% on a sequential basis.

items.statement: FCNR annualized cost at 6.86% vs estimated 7.8% for domestic deposits; 100 bps blended benefit on INR35,000 crores
items.quote: So blend blend between the 6.80% to 7.80%, there is about 100 basis points benefit in having raised this money at the right juncture.

items.statement: Savings account rate reduced to 6% for balances above INR25 lakhs; continuous process of moderating liability costs
items.quote: If you notice that we were earlier paying 7% of savings accounts, then we made 6.5%, then we made 6.25%. Now we made it 6% above INR25 lakhs, we are only paying 6% now.

items.statement: Blended cost of funds for FY28 estimated to increase only 5-10 bps over FY27 despite 50-75 bps repo hikes
items.quote: But overall, overall, I think our own blended cost of funds of FY28, don't take it as a guidance, but I'm just giving you a bit of off -the-cuff estimate that next year should be maybe 3 or 4 or 5 basis points more maybe over this overall cost of funds basis over FY '27.

items.statement: IRDAI consultation paper on insurance commissions could reduce fee income; impact expected to be offset by FCNR benefit, repo hikes and product mix changes
items.quote: We have estimated the impact as is in the current form that if this has to come, this will definitely reduce our fee income. But we feel that, to a large extent, the impact can be offset by the expected repo increase and the FCNR benefit.

items.statement: ECL transition impact broadly neutral on CET-1 ratio when combined with operational risk and credit risk guideline benefits
items.quote: So if we take all RWA changes through this operational risk guideline, credit risk guidelines, offset by capital impacts, which could come through ECL, the impact is broadly sort of neutral on the CET -1 ratio.

items.statement: CAR at 14.66%, CET1 at 13.01% as of September 2026; LCR at 125% average (139% in September due to FCNR inflows)
items.quote: The capital adequacy ratio stood at 14.66% at September with CET1 ratio of 13.01%. On the LCR, the ratio was at 125% on an average for the quarter and with September being at higher at 139%.

items.statement: Excess FCNR liquidity parked in low-yielding instruments; LCR expected to normalize to 115-116% within a month as liquidity deployed
items.quote: As we speak, in October, the further usage of this excess liquidity has happened. And as I said, we should come to the normalized levels of LCR of about 115%, 116% in a month or so.

items.statement: Corporate book: 76% A and above rated, 20% BBB, 4% BB and below; zero delinquency in 7 years on INR1.5 lakh crores disbursed
items.quote: A and above rated companies, since you said what kind of customers we lend to in the corporate side, A and above rated companies, we makes 76% of our book. And BBB companies is 76%. BBB companies is 20% and BB and below is 4%.

items.statement: El Nino and drought in Maharashtra, Karnataka being monitored; no immediate asset quality impact seen for Q3/Q4 but cautious outlook
items.quote: We are, of course, very watchful of this El Niño and the impact will cost to us that a couple of states have declared drought, etcetera. We have to see how much portfolio we have to manage that.

items.statement: Core PAT crossed INR1,000 crores at INR1,036 crores in Q2 FY27; ROA at 0.93%; incremental ROA ~1.8% at 55% cost-to-income
items.quote: This quarter on the core, without any adjustments, it is INR1,036 crores. So we feel good about that. I always said that we'll be in kissing distance of 1% ROA. It looks like we will get there.

items.statement: No dividend or buyback announcements made during the call
items.quote: No, nothing more to add. We've discussed in detail. So thanks very much, everybody.

items.statement: Revenue moderated sequentially in Q2 FY27 due to earlier festive start last year
items.quote: while revenue moderated sequentially in a softer operating due to earlier start of festive last year

items.statement: Operating profit before tax INR1.5 crore vs loss of INR13.3 crore in Q2 FY26
items.quote: As a result, operating profit before tax stood at INR1.5 crores compared with an operating loss of INR13.3 crores in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Total expenses reduced ~20% YoY to INR34.8 crore in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Total expenses stood at INR34.8 crores compared to INR43.3 crores in quarter 2 FY26, a reduction of approximately 20% year -on-year.

items.statement: H1 FY27 operating profit before tax INR5.6 crore vs loss of INR20.2 crore in H1 FY26
items.quote: Operating profit before tax stood at INR5.6 crores compared with an operating loss of INR20.2 crores in H1 FY26.

items.statement: H1 FY27 total expenses reduced ~23% YoY to INR70.4 crore
items.quote: Total expenses stood at INR70.4 crores compared to INR91.7 crores in H1 FY26, a reduction of approximately 23%.

items.statement: Non-FCT revenue split 18-20% of total revenue
items.quote: So currently, 18% to 20% of our revenues come from non -FCT contribution.

items.statement: FCT/NFCT split 80/20 for Q2 FY27
items.quote: NFCT -- 80/20 is the split right now for the quarter.

items.statement: No buyback plans currently
items.quote: So right now, there are no plans.

items.statement: Cannot comment on dividend plans
items.quote: Right now, we cannot comment on that.

items.statement: Quarterly cost run rate around INR39-40 crore expected to continue
items.quote: So, if you see from last 3 quarters, basically, the cost is around this INR39 crores, INR40 crores for the quarter, and that should continue.

items.statement: Total expenses saved ~INR1 crore vs Q1 FY27; employee cost up INR60 lakh, other expenses down INR1.6 crore
items.quote: So, if you see, we are basically INR1 crores -- INR50 lakhs less than the quarter 1 in the total cost, around INR1 crores. That is what we have saved compared to Q1.

items.statement: No guidance for next 2 years due to market and geopolitical uncertainty
items.quote: with the market and the geopolitical uncertainty, right now, we are basically not in a position to give any guidance for the next 2 years.

items.statement: Hoping for better festive in H2 FY27; profitability run rate to continue
items.quote: We are hoping to -- for a better festive than last year, but it again depends on how things move from here.

items.statement: Exploring concerts and events in Tier 2, Tier 3 markets to grow non-FCT revenue
items.quote: We are actually in the process of doing a lot of experiential activities in the Tier 2, Tier 3 markets. We see a lot of traction there. We also have a strong presence there. So, we are exploring concerts and other events in the Tier 2, Tier 3 markets to leverage our strength there.

items.statement: Advertising environment requires measured and client-focused approach
items.quote: The advertising environment continues to require a measured and client-focused approach.

items.statement: Expect flattish credit slippages and credit cost for rest of FY27 despite industry headwinds
items.quote: We expect flattish credit slippages and credit cost for the rest of the year, despite the industry headwinds.

items.statement: Confident of comfortably crossing AUM growth guidance given for FY27
items.quote: we are well poised to continue our strong traction in disbursements in coming quarters, which will help us cross our growth guidance for this year very comfortably

items.statement: Q2FY27 disbursements at Rs 2,078 crores, up 39% QoQ and 74% YoY; AUM at Rs 14,640 crores, up 6.7% QoQ and 14% YoY
items.quote: Our upward trajectory in disbursements continued during the current quarter as well, where we recorded our historical best disbursement of Rs. 2,078 crores, up 39% over previous quarter and 74% year -on-year. The loan book also saw robust growth with our A UM at Rs. 14,640 crores, a growth of over 6.7% over the previous quarter and 14% year -on-year.

items.statement: Collection efficiency improved to 98.2% from 97.7% QoQ; X-bucket collections 99.4% from 99.2%; 30+ DPD down to 11.5% from 12.38%; current bucket up to 84.78% from 83.3%
items.quote: Collections continue to trend very well with our unique customer collection efficiency improving to 98.2% in the current quarter from 97.7% in Q1, along with improvement in X -bucket collections to 99.4% from 99.2% in Q1, which has helped contain forward fl ows. As a result, the current bucket proportion of our A UM rose sharply from 83.3% to 84.78% and 30 plus DPD came down from 12.38% to 11.5%.

items.statement: Slippages eased to 0.68% from 0.70% QoQ; Gross Stage-3 stable at 3.48%; credit cost improved to 1.80% from 1.85%
items.quote: Slippages eased marginally to 0.68% from 0.70% in Q1 and Gross Stage-3 assets were broadly stable at 3.48%, despite macroeconomic headwinds being witnessed across the industry. The credit cost improved to 1.80% of average A UM from 1.85% in Q1.

items.statement: NIM stable at 19.87% vs 19.97% QoQ, up 16 bps YoY; cost of funds on book eased to 8.78% from 8.80%
items.quote: Net interest margin remained broadly stable at 19.87% as against 19.97% in Q1, and was 16 bps higher year-on-year, showing that our spreads have held up despite the drop in yields.

items.statement: Incremental yield hike of ~1% (100 bps) effective Oct 2026 across risk categories; yields to move from 21-23% to 22.5-23.9% range
items.quote: About 1% Nischint, across the various risk characteristics. So the number what was about 21%-23% or so, now we will get to about 22.5% -23.9% thereabouts. So, 1% is the incremental increase across the various types of customers and risk categories.

items.statement: Expect spread compression of 10-15 bps on book cost of funds by FY27 exit due to repo/MCLR repricing; incremental borrowing cost seen at 8.70-8.75% in H2
items.quote: our sense is we should be exiting FY '27 with maybe another 12-15 basis points of higher cost of funds on the book compared to where we are today. So, we are roughly at about 875 or thereabouts. We should possibly be ending the year with more around an 8.90% kind of a number.

items.statement: Incremental debt of Rs 825 crores at all-in cost 8.43%; bank borrowing share 69% vs 67% QoQ; liquidity ~Rs 1,300 crores plus unavailed sanctions ~Rs 1,100 crores
items.quote: We availed incremental debt of Rs. 825 crores during the quarter at an all-inclusive cost of 8.43% and our cost of funds on book eased marginally to 8.78% from 8.80% in Q1.

items.statement: Added 19 branches in Q2, 75 branches over last year; focus on deepening presence in core geographies
items.quote: During this quarter, we added 19 branches, and over the last one year we have added 75 branches, the clear thought being focusing on deepening our presence in our core geographies and also putting up additional branches in those states, where we have been operating for a while and developed good comfort across various aspects.

items.statement: Active loans at ~5.1 lakh, up 5% YoY; ticket size mix targeting 25% sub-3L, 50% 3-5L, 25% 5L+; current mix ~26-27% sub-3L, 51-52% 3-5L
items.quote: Alongside our focus on increasing ticket size, we have also been growing our customer base, with the active loans standing at about 5.1 lakhs, representing a growth of 5% over the previous year.

items.statement: Top-up loans ~10-15% of disbursements (~Rs 200-300 crores); incremental disbursal on top-ups ~50% of outstanding; minimum 12-18 months vintage, no DPD threshold breach, credit score not deteriorated
items.quote: On the top -up part of it, today I will probably say this number is somewhere around 10%-15% of the overall disbursements. So if you have done about Rs. 2,000 crores in the last quarter, possibly the top-up number will be somewhere around Rs. 200-Rs. 300 crores out of this. And roughly, the incremental disbursal on these top-up loans will be anywhere around 50%.

items.statement: October collections trending in line with July/September (98% D1C1); no material state-wise discrepancies; Karnataka collections holding up well vs July/Sept
items.quote: So at the overall level, Viral, we are trending in line with both the July and September numbers, which were good months for us from a collection perspective. October is in line with that. So that leaves us with no cause of concern, anything, because if you compare with September, we still have one more day in October.

items.statement: Stage-2 assets down to Rs 1,173 crores from Rs 1,225 crores YoY; PCR ~40% on Stage-3, ~1.73% on overall AUM; slippages from 61-90 bucket flattish, expect gradual improvement in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: Even in terms of absolute quantum, the overall Stage-2 assets dropped from about Rs. 1,225 crores as of September 30th, 2025 to Rs. 1,173 crores as of September 30th, 2026. Our PCR continues to be at around 40% on the Stage-3 assets and on overall AUM its about 1.73%.

items.statement: Yield increase of 1% on incremental loans will take 24-36 months to fully reflect on book; book is fixed rate so existing yields unchanged
items.quote: Our book is fixed. So, we will not be able to change the rate on the existing book. Fresh disbursements will come in at 1% higher yields. Now, for that to get absorbed on the book will take 8 quarters or so. So you will not see any meaningful impact of the yield increases on the yield for this year, but then it will gradually keep going up.

items.statement: Opex ratio ~7.5% this quarter, ~7.35-7.40% for year; expect 50-75 bps reduction over next couple of years to 6.75-7% via operating leverage
items.quote: Currently, for this quarter, we are roughly about 7.5%. If you look at the year, Sahej, we are about 7.35%-7.40%. Our sense is that this number will trend down at least by 50-75 basis points over the next couple of years. It will take couple of years, but definitely with the operating leverage kicking in, you should see this number somewhere between 6.75%-7%.

items.statement: Written-off loan recovery Rs 13 crores in Q2 (Rs 8 crores Q1); total NPA + write-off recovery ~Rs 35 crores; expect full-year NPA resolution >Rs 100 crores; recovery timeline 18-24 months due to no SARFAESI
items.quote: See, written off accounts, we did about Rs. 13 crores, which is reflecting in the topline. Put together NPAs and written-off accounts, we were at about Rs. 35 odd crores for this quarter.

items.statement: Zero impact from IRDA circular as insurance is pure pass-through; no insurance commission charged to P&L
items.quote: we had zero impact on account of the IRDA ci rcular because we don't charge even a single rupee of insurance commission that comes on to our P&L. Our insurance is a pure pass -through.

items.statement: No drought impact in core states (TN, AP, Telangana >80% AUM); Karnataka collections improved month-on-month, worst behind; MFI overlap 35-40% but better prepared with dedicated collections infra
items.quote: we don't see any kind of drought in these three states. In fact, this month and next month, we see good rains in Tamil Nadu and Andhra and some parts of Telangana, right? So we don't see any kind of drought like situation in these three states.

items.statement: Mudra loans/CGTMSE not overlapping with Five-Star's borrower profile (need GST registration, returns); healthy demand persists for secured mortgage loans
items.quote: But how comfortable are the banks in lending to the profile of borrowers that we are lending to? So this has been a questionable fact and we still have a very healthy demand for our loans. So I don't really see either of them being overlapped because there you also need few other points like proper GST registration, your returns and all that, which possibly are things that we don't insist on.

items.statement: Collection and legal infrastructure fully built out; opex fully absorbs this cost; separate collections team managing arrears book with expertise building
items.quote: The Opex has fully absorbed the impact of the collection infrastructure and both on the collection infrastructure and on the legal infrastructure, the cost has been fully baked in. So from here onwards, you will not see any increase in cost on account of collection or legal infra.

items.statement: Repayment rate 36-37% elevated due to top-up loan accounting change (adjusting outstanding on disbursal); behavioral tenure to normalize closer to 4 years from 4+ years
items.quote: See, what we have done now is we have started to adjust the outstanding on the top- up loans subject to very strong filters from the disbursal of the new loan. So which means a lot of borrowers in the past, we were pushing them that they will have to first close their loan and then take a fresh loan from Five-Star, a top-up loan. So in that scenario, a lot of them would actually fall off because t

items.statement: Variable rate borrowings ~70% of book: 25% MCLR-linked, 30-35% repo/T-Bill linked, 15-18% SOFR/other external benchmarks

items.statement: PAT Rs 299 crores (up 10% QoQ, 5% YoY) including Rs 19 cr one-time tax benefit; ex-one-time PAT up 3% QoQ; ROA 8.39% (+28 bps), ROE 15.25% (+79 bps); H1 PAT Rs 571 crores (+3% YoY)

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 25.5-26.5% for FY27
items.quote: So, as far as the margin guidance is concerned, so we would like to maintain the same guidance , 25.5 to 26.5 %.

items.statement: R&D spend guidance 2.8-3% of revenue for FY27, expected at upper end near 3% including ACTx impact
items.quote: For this fiscal , we expect the R&D spend to be at the upper end of the guidance , which will be close to 3% of the revenue with accounting fo r the impact of ACTx in the R&D.

items.statement: CAPEX guidance 6-7% of revenue for FY27, H1 FY27 at 4.9%
items.quote: The CAPEX as a percentage of revenue is 4. 9% of the total revenue, which is lower than our guidance of 6% to 7% of revenue for FY27.

items.statement: Export growth guidance 20% on constant currency dollar basis for FY27, actual tracking above 30%
items.quote: we gave the guidance of 20% growth rate on a constant currency dollar basis for the export and the actual growth is coming to upward of 30%

items.statement: International business expected to deliver double-digit growth in FY27
items.quote: So, we expect double growth in international business in the Financial Year ‘27.

items.statement: Consumer healthcare growth expected in single digits for FY27, recovery expected in FY28
items.quote: Right now, this year we expect that growth will be in single-digit.

items.statement: MR headcount increase guidance of 7% for FY27, on track

items.statement: Chronic share ambition to add 100-200 bps annually, targeting 50% in 4-5 years
items.quote: our goal and ambition is to add 100 to 200 basis points every year. And our 4 to 5 year ambition is to touch 50%.

items.quote: improving volume growth trend from 0.5% growth in FY25 to 2.3% volume growth in FY26, 4.7% volume growth in 1st Quarter this year to now outperforming IPM with a volume growth of 6. 2% in Quarter 2.

items.quote: Anti-infective continues to recover quarter-on-quarter with a growth of 5.4% in Q2FY27 versus 3.6% in Q1FY27.

items.statement: Hospital segment revenue grew 23% YoY in Q2 FY27
items.quote: During the quarter we saw a strong 23% year-on-year growth in hospital revenues.

items.statement: Consumer healthcare revenue Rs 229 cr in Q2 FY27, impacted by slower offtake and regional weakness in East and South
items.quote: Our consumer healthcare business delivered a revenue of Rs. 229 crores in Q2FY27, impacted by slower offtake in category for the industry and some regional impact in East and South.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 27.1% in Q2 FY27, up 210 bps YoY driven by 90 bps gross margin, 40 bps lower R&D, 80 bps operating leverage

Firstly, the impact of sales price increase which we have taken. Secondly , the favourable sales mix as our chronic contr ibution has increased by 80 basis point on a year -on-year basis. And lastly, there has been a

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 26.7%, up 230 bps YoY from 160 bps gross margin and 70 bps operating leverage
items.quote: The EBITDA margins for H1 F Y27 is 26.7% which has increased by 230 basis point year -on-year basis. The improvement is primarily due to increase in gross margins by 160 basis point and the balance 70% benefit has come from operating leverage.

items.statement: Capex Rs 214 cr in H1 FY27 vs Rs 163 cr in Q2 FY26, at 4.9% of revenue
items.quote: Our CAPEX spent during the quarter has increa sed to Rs. 214 crores in H1 FY27 as compared to Rs. 163 crores in Q2 F Y26. The CAPEX as a percentage of revenue is 4. 9% of the total revenue

items.statement: Net debt reduced to Rs 2,639 cr as of Sep 30, 2026, net debt/EBITDA 0.6x, on track to repay acquisition debt by FY28
items.quote: In line with our prudent financial strategy , we have reduced our net debt to Rs. 2,639 crores as on 30th September 26 resulting in the net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio of 0.6x in Quarter 2 FY27 on trailing 12-month basis. We remain on track to repay the acquisition related debt by FY28.

items.statement: Chronic share ex-BSV expanded 80 bps YoY to 37.4% in Q2 FY27, driven by cardio, anti-diabetic, respiratory outperformance
items.quote: our chronic share excluding BSV expanded by 80 bps year -on-year to 37.4 % led by 1.1x outperformance in cardio and anti -diabetes excluding tirzepatide and a strong 1.9x outp erformance in chronic respiratory during the quarter.

items.statement: New divisions planned in cardio, gastro, dental; Vistaar multi-therapy division expanding
items.quote: While we are expanding our recently launched multi-therapy mass-market division - Vistaar, we are also progressing towards the launch of new divisions in cardio , gastro and dental therapies.

items.quote: we have received a favorable order from the Commissioner of Appeals. So, wherein they have quashed the four years in the order, favorable order has been passed. And the overall exposure has been brought down from the old level by Rs. 300 odd crores.

items.quote: If you see our field force productivity last year was around 7 lakhs and quarter two ending , trailing 12 months is about 7.4 lakhs. So , despite hiring more people , given the growth, we've been able to improve our MR productivity.

items.statement: Monsoon weakness had limited impact as growth driven by chronic, gastro, vitamins not season-dependent

items.quote: Ather inquiries were up even more at about 109%, crossing 10 lakh inquiries for Q2 FY27. And preorders were up at about 108% year-on-year, hitting about 1.8 lakh preorders in Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Wholesale volumes grew 42% YoY to 93,000 units; registrations up 60% YoY to 92,500 units in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Wholesale volume grew from 65,000 units same time last year to 93,000 units in Q2, 42% growth year-on-year.

items.quote: Netting out Q2 FY27 AGM at 24%, which is a 1.6% improvement over Q1 FY27, I think roughly, yes.

So, while there is seasonality in sales, if you look at our historical numbers also, that seasonality does not correspond to seasonality in marketing.

items.statement: GMROI reported around 26% in H1 FY27, lower than FY25/FY26 due to low average store age; full GMROI extraction visible only when stores reach vintage; old cohort data shows underlying GMROI

So, we are looking at all the avenues to bring that cost of debt down. So, it's largely primary objective is for looking at the debt stack, blended cost of debt, and some high-cost debt to be retired.

items.quote: Making gold, actually, is changing atoms at a nuclear level, which is actually playing with neutrons and protons in a nucleus of an atom. Now, that is something that has never been done on planet Earth except in fusio n reactors, which actually produce

items.statement: Flagship store launched at Park Street, Kolkata as experiment to expand product lines beyond casted jewellery into handmade, Kundan techniques; may try 1-2 more stores before strategizing

items.statement: Revenue target of INR 12,000 crores by 2030; funding via internal accruals from vintage store maturation, low net debt-to-equity, and growing customer advances/schemes; no equity capital raise seen as necessary
items.quote: as the vintage of the store picks up, the capital productivity of those stores and ROICs and the internal accruals that those stores generate continue to Q2FY27 | Earnings Call Transcript move up. items.statement: Growth trends broad-based across Tier-1, Tier-2, Tier-3 cities; no behavioural difference; benefiting from omnichannel shift, lightweight jewellery trend, and unorganized-to-organized shift

items.statement: No target product mix; studded vs non-studded mix is consumer-driven outcome; GMROI similar across categories due to margin-turn trade-off; focus on ROIC/GMROI not margin mix
items.quote: So, a studded has a higher margin, but generally a lower turn. Non - studded has lower margin, but much higher turn. So, the capital productivity that you get from these two is a function of the brand, the pricing power, and thus the GMROIs are not very

items.statement: Repeat customer growth is strong, not flattish; repeat AOVs naturally higher due to younger acquisition age and income curve; new customer growth improving after entry-level price point corrections started in Q3 last year

items.statement: No change to 50% hedging policy; operating as communicated
